===== agentic-juror.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# agentic-juror.sh <worktree> <sha> <outprefix> — one foreign-lineage model reviews a
     3	# commit AGENTICALLY (reads callers/config beyond the diff), Codex-style.
     4	# Harness: headless Claude Code pointed at OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint
     5	# (/api/v1/messages passes tool_use through — probed 2026-07-05). Model: GLM-5.2.
     6	# Read-only: enforced with --disallowedTools (deny beats allow). NOTE (10-commit bench
     7	# lesson): --allowedTools alone does NOT restrict — the worktree inherits the repo's
     8	# .claude/settings.json allow rules, so the model also ran grep/npx/curl. Zero writes
     9	# occurred in 10/10 runs, but always verify the writes_check line in the .meta output.
    10	# Proven in the 2026-07-05 smoke test (2 commits, 25 tool calls, 0 format failures,
    11	# 0 writes, ~$0.21-0.41/review): caught the reduced-motion diffBaseline bug diff-only
    12	# GLM missed, plus a new real argv bug. Known wart: `claude -p` result field comes back
    13	# EMPTY (GLM ends with a thinking block) — read the final text from the session
    14	# transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<worktree-slug>/*.jsonl instead.
    15	# ponytail: 2-run smoke evidence, not a reliability study — promote to a standing lane
    16	# only after a 10-commit bench like the diff-only one.
    17	set -uo pipefail
    18	WT="$1"; SHA="$2"; OUT="$3"
    19	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    20	KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}"
    21	[ -n "$KEY" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    22	
    23	credits() { curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/credits -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin)["data"];print(d["total_credits"]-d["total_usage"])'; }
    24	
    25	BEFORE=$(credits); echo "credits_before=$BEFORE" > "$OUT.meta"
    26	START=$(date +%s)
    27	
    28	PROMPT="You are reviewing commit $SHA in this git repo for CORRECTNESS bugs and security issues only — not style. First run: git show $SHA  to see the diff. Then USE THE REPO: read the full files the diff touches and any callers/config they interact with, to verify each suspicion against the real code beyond the diff hunks. Report each finding as P1 (blocking) / P2 (likely bug) / P3 (minor) with file:line and one concrete failing input/state. If part of the diff is correct, don't invent problems. Finish with a FINDINGS list."
    29	
    30	# CLAUDE_AUTOCAPTURE=1 marks this as pipeline-internal so the session-memory hooks
    31	# skip it (inferred from brain-consolidate.sh's use; unmarked smoke runs each spawned
    32	# a ~$0.12 distill child and polluted the auto notes — verify on next run).
    33	cd "$WT" && CLAUDE_AUTOCAPTURE=1 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api" \
    34	  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$KEY" \
    35	  ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$KEY" \
    36	  ANTHROPIC_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.2" \
    37	  ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.2" \
    38	  CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 \
    39	  timeout 900 claude -p "$PROMPT" \
    40	    --model "z-ai/glm-5.2" \
    41	    --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob,Bash(git show:*),Bash(git log:*),Bash(git diff:*),Bash(cat:*),Bash(ls:*)" \
    42	    --disallowedTools "Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,Task,Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*),Bash(git push:*),Bash(rm:*),Bash(mv:*),Bash(npm install:*),Bash(npx convex:*)" \
    43	    --max-turns 40 \
    44	    --output-format json > "$OUT.json" 2> "$OUT.err"
    45	RC=$?
    46	
    47	AFTER=$(credits)
    48	{ echo "credits_after=$AFTER"
    49	  echo "exit_code=$RC"
    50	  echo "wall_seconds=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))"
    51	  echo "writes_check=$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain | wc -l) dirty files"
    52	} >> "$OUT.meta"
    53	echo "done $SHA rc=$RC"
===== hooks/pre-push =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# pre-push — refuse to publish per-user private notes to a PUBLIC remote.
     3	#
     4	# Why a hook and not just .gitignore: untracking a file at HEAD does NOT remove it
     5	# from older commits. idea-ledger.md was untracked at the tip on 2026-07-27 while two
     6	# unpushed commits still carried the blob — one `git push` would have published it.
     7	# So this checks every commit in the push RANGE, not just the tip.
     8	#
     9	# INSTALL (git never auto-runs hooks from a clone — this is a git security property,
    10	# not an oversight here):  git config core.hooksPath hooks
    11	# jury-check.sh reports every session whether this guard is actually active.
    12	#
    13	# ponytail: one explicit list, no config file. Add names to PRIVATE as they appear.
    14	set -uo pipefail
    15	
    16	# git passes <remote-name> <remote-url>. Excluding commits present on a hardcoded
    17	# "origin" is wrong when pushing to a DIFFERENT remote: with an internal origin and
    18	# a public remote, everything already on origin was skipped and the private file
    19	# published (review-gate P1, 07-27). An unknown/URL remote matches no refs, so the
    20	# scan widens rather than narrows — the safe direction.
    21	REMOTE="${1:-origin}"
    22	
    23	# Match the BASENAME at ANY depth, because .gitignore does: a bare pattern with no
    24	# slash is ignored at every level, so notes/idea-ledger.md is private to git but was
    25	# publishable by this guard — the exact inverse of the round-1 claim I refuted.
    26	PRIVATE='(^|/)(idea-ledger\.md|[^/]*\.private\.md)$'
    27	Z=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
    28	bad=0
    29	
    30	while read -r _lref lsha _rref rsha; do
    31	  [ "$lsha" = "$Z" ] && continue                      # branch deletion — nothing to inspect
    32	  # FAIL CLOSED. Discarding rev-list's exit status made this guard fail OPEN: an
    33	  # advertised remote SHA that is not present locally (shallow / partial fetch)
    34	  # makes rev-list exit 128, the commit list comes back empty, the loop never
    35	  # runs, and a push carrying private notes is ALLOWED. Caught by review-gate
    36	  # 2026-07-27 by executing it, not by reading it. An unknown range is not an
    37	  # empty range — if we cannot enumerate what is being pushed, we refuse.
    38	  if [ "$rsha" = "$Z" ]; then
    39	    # Scan EVERYTHING reachable. Excluding commits that local remote-tracking refs
    40	    # claim are already published is unsound: those refs go stale, and survive the
    41	    # remote being repointed at a different URL — so a commit "already on origin"
    42	    # may never have been on THIS remote. Reproduced by review-gate, 07-27.
    43	    # ponytail: O(history) per new-branch push; fine at this repo's size. If it ever
    44	    # matters, ask the remote itself with ls-remote rather than trusting local refs.
    45	    raw="$(git rev-list "$lsha" 2>&1)" || raw="!"
    46	  else
    47	    raw="$(git rev-list "$rsha..$lsha" 2>&1)" || raw="!"
    48	  fi
    49	  if [ "$raw" = "!" ]; then
    50	    printf '✗ pre-push BLOCKED — cannot enumerate the push range (%s..%s).\n' "${rsha:0:7}" "${lsha:0:7}" >&2
    51	    printf '      Refusing rather than assuming it is empty. Try: git fetch origin\n' >&2
    52	    bad=1; continue
    53	  fi
    54	  mapfile -t commits <<< "$raw"
    55	  for c in "${commits[@]}"; do
    56	    [ -n "$c" ] || continue
    57	    # -z: git C-QUOTES non-ASCII/special names by default ("\345\256\242...\.md"),
    58	    # which the regex misses — a real leak path for e.g. 客户.private.md.
    59	    # NUL-delimited output is raw. (review-gate P1, 07-27)
    60	    # tr INSIDE the pipeline: bash command substitution silently strips NUL bytes,
    61	    # so capturing -z output directly concatenates every path into one line and the
    62	    # anchored regex stops matching. pipefail carries an ls-tree failure out.
    63	    if ! tree="$(git ls-tree -r -z --name-only "$c" 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n')"; then
    64	      printf '✗ pre-push BLOCKED — cannot read the tree of %s; refusing to assume it is clean\n' "${c:0:7}" >&2
    65	      bad=1; continue
    66	    fi
    67	    hits="$(printf '%s\n' "$tree" | grep -E "$PRIVATE" || true)"
    68	    if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
    69	      printf '✗ pre-push BLOCKED — %s carries private file(s):\n' "${c:0:7}" >&2
    70	      printf '%s\n' "$hits" | sed 's/^/      /' >&2
    71	      bad=1
    72	    fi
    73	  done
    74	done
    75	
    76	if [ "$bad" != 0 ]; then
    77	  cat >&2 <<'MSG'
    78	
    79	  This remote is PUBLIC. Untracking the file at HEAD is not enough — the blob is
    80	  still in the commits being pushed. Drop it from the range first, e.g.:
    81	
    82	    git filter-branch --index-filter 'git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch <file>' <upstream>..HEAD
    83	
    84	  where <upstream> is what you are pushing against (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u}).
    85	
    86	  Then push again. To bypass deliberately: git push --no-verify (think first).
    87	MSG
    88	  exit 1
    89	fi
    90	exit 0
===== idea-options.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# idea-options.sh — the GENERATE stage the planning pipeline was missing.
     3	#
     4	# idea-panel.sh answers "is this idea any good?" — its three roles (advocate,
     5	# skeptic, researcher) all REACT to the solution you hand them, so by
     6	# construction it can never tell you there is a better idea. That gap was found
     7	# on 2026-07-25: asked for an alternative to a proposed mobile UI, the pipeline
     8	# had no seat for one and produced only a critique of the original.
     9	#
    10	# This script takes the PROBLEM and produces DIVERGENT APPROACHES to it:
    11	#   0. brain-search prior knowledge + read the decision ledger (your taste)
    12	#   1. N proposers, different lineages, IN PARALLEL and blind to each other —
    13	#      each must propose ONE approach in a fixed shape. If the problem statement
    14	#      names a solution already, they are required to propose a DIFFERENT one.
    15	#   2. one judge scores every option on the same rubric and ranks them
    16	#   3. synthesis: a recommendation, what to graft from the runners-up, and the
    17	#      checks to run before committing
    18	#   4. append to the shared idea-ledger
    19	#
    20	# Usage:  idea-options.sh problem.md ["optional focus"]
    21	#         echo "the problem..." | idea-options.sh -
    22	#
    23	# Then log your pick:  idea-decide "<ref>" "<what you chose and why>"
    24	#
    25	# Env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (req). MODELS_PROPOSERS (comma-sep) / MODELS_JUDGE /
    26	#      MODELS_SYNTH override the defaults. PANEL_TIMEOUT (default 240s).
    27	set -uo pipefail
    28	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    29	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    30	[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    31	
    32	SRC="${1:--}"; FOCUS="${2:-}"
    33	CONTENT="$([ "$SRC" = "-" ] && cat || cat "$SRC")"
    34	[ -n "$CONTENT" ] || { echo "✗ empty problem statement" >&2; exit 1; }
    35	MAX=${MAX_CHARS:-40000}; CONTENT="${CONTENT:0:$MAX}"
    36	
    37	# Proposers sit in cheap/diverse seats (their job is RANGE, not judgement);
    38	# the proven judge model holds the scoring seat, same split as idea-panel.
    39	IFS=, read -r -a PROPOSERS <<< "${MODELS_PROPOSERS:-deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash,google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite,minimax/minimax-m3}"
    40	M_JUDGE="${MODELS_JUDGE:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
    41	M_SYNTH="${MODELS_SYNTH:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
    42	
    43	call() { # model, prompt  ->  text   (verbatim from idea-panel.sh — same wire shape)
    44	  local model="$1" prompt="$2" req
    45	  req=$(python3 -c '
    46	import json,sys
    47	print(json.dumps({"model":sys.argv[3],"temperature":0,
    48	  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":sys.argv[1]+"\n\n--- PROBLEM ---\n"+sys.argv[2]}]}))' \
    49	    "$prompt" "$CONTENT" "$model")
    50	  curl -s -m "${PANEL_TIMEOUT:-240}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
    51	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    52	    -H "X-Title: idea-options" -d "$req" | python3 -c '
    53	import json,sys
    54	raw=sys.stdin.read()
    55	try: d=json.loads(raw)
    56	except Exception: print("(non-JSON response)"); sys.exit(1)
    57	if isinstance(d,dict) and d.get("error"): print("(model error:",d["error"],")"); sys.exit(1)
    58	try:
    59	  m=d["choices"][0]["message"]; body=m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning")
    60	  if not body: print("(empty response)"); sys.exit(1)
    61	  print(body)
    62	except Exception: print("(bad shape:",raw[:200],")"); sys.exit(1)'
    63	}
    64	
    65	FOCUS_LINE="${FOCUS:+ Focus on: $FOCUS.}"
    66	
    67	# The fixed output shape is what makes options comparable — a judge cannot rank
    68	# free-form prose on the same axes.
    69	SHAPE='Answer in EXACTLY this shape, once:
    70	
    71	### OPTION: <short distinctive name>
    72	MECHANISM: <how it actually works, concretely — name the moving parts>
    73	WHY IT FITS: <why this solves the stated problem, not a nearby one>
    74	COST: <build effort + ongoing cost; be honest about the expensive part>
    75	BREAKS/RISKS: <what this makes worse, who it hurts, what could regress>
    76	REVERSIBILITY: <how hard to undo once shipped>
    77	EVIDENCE NEEDED: <the check that would confirm this is the right call>'
    78	
    79	P_PROPOSE="You are a solution ARCHITECT. Propose ONE approach that solves the PROBLEM below.
    80	
    81	HARD RULES:
    82	- Solve the PROBLEM, not a nearby or easier one.
    83	- If the problem statement mentions a solution someone already proposed, you MUST propose a DIFFERENT approach. Do not endorse, restate, or merely refine theirs.
    84	- Do NOT critique other approaches. Do NOT hedge with several options. ONE approach, committed to.
    85	- Prefer approaches that a small team can ship. Name the cheapest version that still solves it.
    86	- No filler. If a section is genuinely 'none', say none.${FOCUS_LINE}
    87	
    88	$SHAPE"
    89	
    90	echo "◆ idea-options: ledger → ${#PROPOSERS[@]} blind proposers → judge($M_JUDGE) → synthesis" >&2
    91	
    92	# ── 0. PRIOR KNOWLEDGE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    93	echo "═══ 0 · PRIOR KNOWLEDGE (brain-search) ═══"
    94	TERMS=$(python3 -c '
    95	import re,sys,collections
    96	stop=set("this that with have from your will they them then than into over about which what when where would could should being your yours idea plan system user users problem".split())
    97	w=[x.lower() for x in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]{5,}", sys.stdin.read())]
    98	c=collections.Counter(x for x in w if x not in stop)
    99	print(" ".join(t for t,_ in c.most_common(4)))' <<<"$CONTENT")
   100	echo "  terms: $TERMS"
   101	python3 /root/.claude/scripts/brain-search.py -n 4 $TERMS 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /' || echo "  (no ledger hits)"
   102	
   103	PRIOR_DECISIONS="$(grep -A2 '^### DECISION' "$HERE/idea-ledger.md" 2>/dev/null | tail -40 || true)"
   104	[ -n "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" ] && { echo; echo "  prior decisions on record (feeding synthesis):"; echo "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" | sed 's/^/    /'; }
   105	
   106	# ── 1. BLIND PROPOSERS (parallel) ────────────────────────────────────────────
   107	TMP=$(mktemp -d) || TMP=""
   108	{ [ -n "$TMP" ] && [ -d "$TMP" ]; } || { echo "✗ mktemp -d failed — refusing to run" >&2; exit 2; }; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
   109	i=0
   110	for m in "${PROPOSERS[@]}"; do
   111	  i=$((i+1))
   112	  ( call "$m" "$P_PROPOSE" > "$TMP/opt$i" 2>&1 || touch "$TMP/opt$i.fail" ) &
   113	done
   114	wait
   115	
   116	echo; echo "═══ 1 · OPTIONS (each proposed blind) ═══"
   117	i=0; BUNDLE=""
   118	for m in "${PROPOSERS[@]}"; do
   119	  i=$((i+1))
   120	  echo; echo "── proposer $i ($m) ──"; cat "$TMP/opt$i"
   121	  BUNDLE="$BUNDLE
   122	
   123	=== FROM PROPOSER $i ($m) ===
   124	$(cat "$TMP/opt$i")"
   125	done
   126	
   127	# ── 2. JUDGE — same rubric applied to every option ───────────────────────────
   128	P_JUDGE="Below are independently-proposed approaches to the same problem.
   129	
   130	First, MERGE duplicates: if two proposers describe the same approach, treat them as one option and say so. Genuinely distinct approaches stay separate.
   131	
   132	Then score EVERY surviving option 1-5 on each axis, with a one-line reason per score:
   133	- FIT — does it solve the stated problem, or a nearby easier one?
   134	- COST — build + ongoing (5 = cheap)
   135	- REVERSIBILITY — how easily undone (5 = trivial to undo)
   136	- CONFIDENCE — how much do we already know this works, vs needing evidence?
   137	
   138	Then rank them by total, and state in one line WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE for the bottom-ranked option to beat the top one. Be terse. Do not invent new options."
   139	
   140	echo; echo "═══ 2 · SCORED ($M_JUDGE) ═══"
   141	if compgen -G "$TMP/*.fail" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   142	  echo >&2; echo "✗ proposer(s) FAILED above — refusing to judge/rank error text," >&2
   143	  echo "  and NOT appending to the ledger." >&2; exit 1
   144	fi
   145	SCORES=$(call "$M_JUDGE" "$(printf '%s' "$BUNDLE")
   146	
   147	$P_JUDGE") || { echo "✗ judge failed — NOT ranking or appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
   148	echo "$SCORES"
   149	
   150	# ── 3. SYNTHESIS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   151	P_SYNTH="You have independently-proposed options and a judge's scoring of them.
   152	
   153	Produce, terse:
   154	1. RECOMMENDATION — one option, and the single strongest reason it wins.
   155	2. GRAFT — the best specific idea from a NON-winning option that should be folded into the winner.
   156	3. DO NOT BUILD — any option that looks attractive but should be rejected, and why in one line.
   157	4. BEFORE COMMITTING — the concrete checks to run first (each must be mechanically checkable).
   158	Do not restate the options. Decide.${PRIOR_DECISIONS:+
   159	
   160	The user has made these PRIOR DECISIONS (their taste signal) — weight toward what they have valued, and FLAG if a recommendation contradicts one:
   161	$PRIOR_DECISIONS}"
   162	
   163	echo; echo "═══ 3 · SYNTHESIS ($M_SYNTH) ═══"
   164	OUT=$(call "$M_SYNTH" "$(printf '%s' "$BUNDLE")
   165	
   166	JUDGE SAID:
   167	$SCORES
   168	
   169	$P_SYNTH") || { echo "✗ synthesis failed — NOT appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
   170	echo "$OUT"
   171	
   172	# ── 4. LEDGER ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   173	LEDGER="$HERE/idea-ledger.md"
   174	{ echo; echo "## OPTIONS — $(head -1 <<<"$CONTENT" | sed 's/^#* *//' | cut -c1-80)"
   175	  echo "_proposers: ${PROPOSERS[*]} · judge=$M_JUDGE · synth=${M_SYNTH}_"
   176	  echo "$SCORES"; echo; echo "$OUT"; echo "---"; } >> "$LEDGER" || { echo "✗ ledger append FAILED — not reporting success" >&2; exit 1; }
   177	echo; echo "◆ appended to $LEDGER — log your pick with: idea-decide \"<ref>\" \"<choice + why>\"" >&2
===== idea-panel.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# idea-panel.sh — the divergence-map front end for an idea/plan.
     3	#
     4	# Not "N models critique in parallel" (that's panel.sh). This surfaces WHERE
     5	# diverse perspectives DISAGREE — because disagreement is the signal worth
     6	# researching. Pipeline:
     7	#   0. LEDGER FIRST — brain-search the idea's terms; a prior verdict beats a
     8	#      fresh debate (the 2026-07-24 lesson: the vault already had the answer).
     9	#   1. Three ROLE-diverse, LINEAGE-diverse perspectives: advocate / skeptic /
    10	#      researcher (role framing changes output — proven in the bake-off).
    11	#   2. Synthesis into a DIVERGENCE MAP: consensus | disagreements+crux | unknowns.
    12	#   3. Append to the idea-ledger for later preference/reliability learning.
    13	#
    14	# Usage:  idea-panel.sh idea.md ["optional focus"]
    15	#         echo "my idea..." | idea-panel.sh -
    16	#
    17	# Env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (req). MODELS_ADVOCATE/SKEPTIC/RESEARCHER/SYNTH override roles.
    18	set -euo pipefail
    19	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    20	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    21	[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    22	
    23	SRC="${1:--}"; FOCUS="${2:-}"
    24	CONTENT="$([ "$SRC" = "-" ] && cat || cat "$SRC")"
    25	[ -n "$CONTENT" ] || { echo "✗ empty idea" >&2; exit 1; }
    26	MAX=${MAX_CHARS:-40000}; CONTENT="${CONTENT:0:$MAX}"
    27	
    28	# Role→model. Candidates (deepseek-v4-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite) sit in the
    29	# generative roles so each run measures their PLANNING signal; the proven
    30	# critic/synth models (minimax, glm) hold the judgement seats.
    31	M_ADV="${MODELS_ADVOCATE:-deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash}"
    32	M_SKEP="${MODELS_SKEPTIC:-minimax/minimax-m3}"
    33	M_RES="${MODELS_RESEARCHER:-google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite}"
    34	M_SYNTH="${MODELS_SYNTH:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
    35	
    36	call() { # model, prompt  ->  text
    37	  local model="$1" prompt="$2" req
    38	  req=$(python3 -c '
    39	import json,sys
    40	print(json.dumps({"model":sys.argv[3],"temperature":0,
    41	  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":sys.argv[1]+"\n\n--- IDEA ---\n"+sys.argv[2]}]}))' \
    42	    "$prompt" "$CONTENT" "$model")
    43	  curl -s -m "${PANEL_TIMEOUT:-240}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
    44	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    45	    -H "X-Title: idea-panel" -d "$req" | python3 -c '
    46	import json,sys
    47	raw=sys.stdin.read()
    48	try: d=json.loads(raw)
    49	except Exception: print("(non-JSON response)"); sys.exit(1)
    50	if isinstance(d,dict) and d.get("error"): print("(model error:",d["error"],")"); sys.exit(1)
    51	try:
    52	  m=d["choices"][0]["message"]; body=m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning")
    53	  if not body: print("(empty response)"); sys.exit(1)
    54	  print(body)
    55	except Exception: print("(bad shape:",raw[:200],")"); sys.exit(1)'
    56	}
    57	
    58	FOCUS_LINE="${FOCUS:+ The user asks you to focus on: $FOCUS.}"
    59	P_ADV="You are an ADVOCATE. You believe this idea can work. Give the STRONGEST version: the core mechanism, why it succeeds, the best realistic path to make it real, and the one thing that most makes it worth doing. Be concrete, not cheerleading.$FOCUS_LINE"
    60	P_SKEP="You are a SKEPTIC. You think this idea is likely flawed. Find the CONCRETE reasons it fails: unit-economics that don't add up (do the math), internal contradictions, hidden costs, false assumptions, why it won't work as imagined, simpler things that already solve it. No vague doubts — specific failure modes only.$FOCUS_LINE"
    61	P_RES="You are a RESEARCHER. Do NOT judge good/bad. Identify what is UNKNOWN: the load-bearing ASSUMPTIONS that need checking, the QUESTIONS whose answers would flip the verdict, and for each, HOW to find the answer (what to test, measure, or look up). Rank by how much the answer would change the decision.$FOCUS_LINE"
    62	
    63	echo "◆ idea-panel: ledger → advocate($M_ADV) · skeptic($M_SKEP) · researcher($M_RES) → divergence map" >&2
    64	
    65	# ── 0. LEDGER FIRST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    66	echo "═══ 0 · PRIOR KNOWLEDGE (brain-search) ═══"
    67	TERMS=$(python3 -c '
    68	import re,sys,collections
    69	stop=set("this that with have from your will they them then than into over about which what when where would could should being your yours idea plan system user users".split())
    70	w=[x.lower() for x in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]{5,}", sys.stdin.read())]
    71	c=collections.Counter(x for x in w if x not in stop)
    72	print(" ".join(t for t,_ in c.most_common(4)))' <<<"$CONTENT")
    73	echo "  terms: $TERMS"
    74	python3 /root/.claude/scripts/brain-search.py -n 4 $TERMS 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /' || echo "  (no ledger hits)"
    75	
    76	# Prior DECISIONS (your logged picks + why) — the taste signal fed into synthesis.
    77	PRIOR_DECISIONS="$(grep -A2 '^### DECISION' "$HERE/idea-ledger.md" 2>/dev/null | tail -40 || true)"
    78	[ -n "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" ] && { echo; echo "  prior decisions on record (feeding synthesis):"; echo "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" | sed 's/^/    /'; }
    79	
    80	# ── 1. THREE ROLE-DIVERSE PERSPECTIVES (parallel) ────────────────────────────
    81	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
    82	( call "$M_ADV"  "$P_ADV"  > "$TMP/adv"  2>&1 || touch "$TMP/adv.fail"  ) &
    83	( call "$M_SKEP" "$P_SKEP" > "$TMP/skep" 2>&1 || touch "$TMP/skep.fail" ) &
    84	( call "$M_RES"  "$P_RES"  > "$TMP/res"  2>&1 || touch "$TMP/res.fail"  ) &
    85	wait
    86	echo; echo "═══ 1 · PERSPECTIVES ═══"
    87	for r in "ADVOCATE:$M_ADV:adv" "SKEPTIC:$M_SKEP:skep" "RESEARCHER:$M_RES:res"; do
    88	  IFS=: read -r label model file <<<"$r"
    89	  echo; echo "── $label ($model) ──"; cat "$TMP/$file"
    90	done
    91	
    92	# A map synthesized from error strings is indistinguishable from a real one once
    93	# it is in the ledger. If any perspective failed, stop here (review-gate P2, 07-27).
    94	if compgen -G "$TMP/*.fail" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    95	  echo >&2; echo "✗ perspective(s) FAILED above — refusing to synthesize a divergence map" >&2
    96	  echo "  from error text, and NOT appending to the ledger." >&2; exit 1
    97	fi
    98	
    99	# ── 2. DIVERGENCE MAP ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   100	# %s not %b: model output is untrusted and %b would interpret its backslash
   101	# escapes — a returned "\\c" truncates the bundle silently. (review-gate P2, 07-27)
   102	BUNDLE="$(printf 'ADVOCATE said:\n%s\n\nSKEPTIC said:\n%s\n\nRESEARCHER said:\n%s\n' \
   103	  "$(cat "$TMP/adv")" "$(cat "$TMP/skep")" "$(cat "$TMP/res")")"
   104	P_SYNTH="Below are three perspectives (advocate/skeptic/researcher) on the same idea. Produce a DIVERGENCE MAP, nothing else:
   105	1. CONSENSUS — points all three implicitly agree on (the safe ground).
   106	2. DISAGREEMENTS — where they genuinely conflict. For EACH, state the CRUX: the single question whose answer decides who is right.
   107	3. TOP UNKNOWNS TO RESEARCH — ranked by how much resolving them would change the decision; name the concrete check for each.
   108	Be terse and concrete. Do not re-argue the idea; map the structure of the disagreement.${PRIOR_DECISIONS:+
   109	
   110	The user has made these PRIOR DECISIONS on related ideas (their taste signal) — weight the map toward what they have valued, and FLAG if this idea repeats or contradicts a past decision:
   111	$PRIOR_DECISIONS}"
   112	echo; echo "═══ 2 · DIVERGENCE MAP ($M_SYNTH) ═══"
   113	MAP=$(call "$M_SYNTH" "$BUNDLE
   114	
   115	$P_SYNTH") || {
   116	  echo "✗ synthesis failed — NOT appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
   117	echo "$MAP"
   118	
   119	# ── 3. LEDGER APPEND (capture for later learning) ────────────────────────────
   120	LEDGER="$HERE/idea-ledger.md"
   121	{ echo; echo "## $(head -1 <<<"$CONTENT" | sed 's/^#* *//' | cut -c1-80) — logged"
   122	  echo "_models: adv=$M_ADV skep=$M_SKEP res=$M_RES synth=${M_SYNTH}_"
   123	  echo "$MAP"; echo "---"; } >> "$LEDGER" || { echo "✗ ledger append FAILED — not reporting success" >&2; exit 1; }
   124	echo; echo "◆ appended to $LEDGER (add your pick + why later → feeds preference learning)" >&2
===== juror.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# juror.sh — one AI model reviews a git diff for correctness/security bugs.
     3	#
     4	# Reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the env and sends the diff to one model via
     5	# OpenRouter (any model, one API). Read-only: it prints findings, it never edits
     6	# your code. Triage the findings yourself — treat them as leads, not verdicts.
     7	#
     8	# Usage (run from inside a git repo):
     9	#   juror.sh                     # branch diff vs origin/main (or origin/master)
    10	#   juror.sh --base <ref>        # diff vs an arbitrary base ref
    11	#   juror.sh --commit <sha>      # a single commit
    12	#   juror.sh --uncommitted       # your current uncommitted (tracked) changes
    13	#   juror.sh "<focus note>"      # append a focus instruction to the prompt
    14	#
    15	# Env:
    16	#   OPENROUTER_API_KEY   required
    17	#   MODEL                OpenRouter model slug (default: z-ai/glm-5.2 — it won the
    18	#                        benchmark in ./bench; verify slugs at openrouter.ai/models)
    19	#   MAX_DIFF_CHARS       truncate very large diffs (default 120000)
    20	#   REVIEW_TIMEOUT       per-model seconds (default 280 — high enough for slow
    21	#                        reasoning models like deepseek-v4-pro on a large diff)
    22	set -euo pipefail
    23	
    24	# --help must work without a key or a repo.
    25	case "${1:-}" in -h|--help) grep '^#' "$0" | grep -v '^#!' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;; esac
    26	
    27	MODEL="${MODEL:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
    28	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    29	KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}"
    30	MAX="${MAX_DIFF_CHARS:-120000}"
    31	[ -n "$KEY" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    32	git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "✗ not in a git repo" >&2; exit 1; }
    33	
    34	MODE=""; BASE=""; FOCUS=""
    35	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --base) MODE="base"; BASE="$2"; shift 2;;
    38	    --commit) MODE="commit"; BASE="$2"; shift 2;;
    39	    --uncommitted) MODE="uncommitted"; shift;;
    40	    -h|--help) grep '^#' "$0" | grep -v '^#!' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;;
    41	    *) FOCUS="$1"; shift;;
    42	  esac
    43	done
    44	
    45	# Default: diff the branch against its upstream default branch.
    46	if [ -z "$MODE" ]; then
    47	  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
    48	    MODE="uncommitted"
    49	  else
    50	    MODE="base"; BASE="origin/main"
    51	    git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1 || BASE="origin/master"
    52	  fi
    53	fi
    54	
    55	case "$MODE" in
    56	  uncommitted) DIFF=$(git diff HEAD); SCOPE="uncommitted changes";;
    57	  base)        DIFF=$(git diff "$BASE"...HEAD); SCOPE="branch vs $BASE";;
    58	  commit)      DIFF=$(git show "$BASE"); SCOPE="commit $BASE";;
    59	esac
    60	[ -n "$DIFF" ] || { echo "◆ nothing to review ($SCOPE)"; exit 0; }
    61	echo "◆ $MODEL reviewing: $SCOPE ($(printf '%s' "$DIFF" | grep -c '^[+-]') changed lines)" >&2
    62	
    63	PROMPT="You are a senior code reviewer. Review this git diff for CORRECTNESS bugs and security issues only — not style. Tag each finding P1 (blocking correctness) / P2 (likely bug) / P3 (minor), each with file:line and one line of concrete evidence: a specific input or state that produces a wrong output. If the diff is correct, say so plainly. Be precise — false positives waste the maintainer's time.${FOCUS:+ Focus: $FOCUS}"
    64	
    65	# Build the JSON body with python so an arbitrary diff can't break quoting.
    66	REQ=$(python3 -c '
    67	import json,sys
    68	prompt, diff, model, mx = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4])
    69	print(json.dumps({
    70	  "model": model,
    71	  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt + "\n\n```diff\n" + diff[:mx] + "\n```"}],
    72	  "temperature": 0,
    73	}))' "$PROMPT" "$DIFF" "$MODEL" "$MAX")
    74	
    75	# OpenRouter drops ~4% of calls (truncated/non-JSON; measured 2026-07-05, 7/7 recovered
    76	# on one retry) — so try twice before reporting an error.
    77	run_review() {
    78	  curl -s -m "${REVIEW_TIMEOUT:-280}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
    79	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    80	    -H "X-Title: AI Review Jury" \
    81	    -d "$REQ" | python3 -c '
    82	import json,sys
    83	raw = sys.stdin.read()
    84	try:
    85	  d = json.loads(raw)
    86	except Exception as e:
    87	  print("✗ non-JSON response ("+str(e)+"); first 300 chars:"); print(raw[:300]); sys.exit(1)
    88	if isinstance(d, dict) and d.get("error"):
    89	  print("✗ model error:", d["error"]); sys.exit(1)
    90	try:
    91	  m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
    92	  # reasoning models sometimes route the answer via reasoning/reasoning_content
    93	  txt = m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning_content") or m.get("reasoning") or ""
    94	except Exception:
    95	  print("✗ unexpected response shape; first 300 chars:"); print(raw[:300]); sys.exit(1)
    96	print(txt if txt else "(empty response)")'
    97	}
    98	OUT="$(run_review)"
    99	if printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -q '^✗\|^(empty response)$'; then
   100	  echo "◆ retrying $MODEL (bad response)" >&2
   101	  OUT="$(run_review)"
   102	fi
   103	printf '%s\n' "$OUT"
===== jury-check.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# jury-check.sh — 5-second health check: is the jury wired, current, and live?
     3	# Run at the start of a session to confirm /jury is set up within normal parameters.
     4	set -uo pipefail
     5	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
     6	ok=0; bad=0
     7	say(){ printf "  %s %s\n" "$1" "$2"; [ "$1" = "✓" ] && ok=$((ok+1)) || bad=$((bad+1)); }
     8	
     9	# ONE definition, used by the check AND by --selftest, so they cannot drift.
    10	# SHA equality (the original) cannot tell ahead from behind: it printed "BEHIND —
    11	# git pull" at a checkout sitting on unpushed commits, which is the only direction
    12	# that can publish something. Fixtures below prove all four states.
    13	sync_state(){ # repo -> sync | "ahead N" | "behind N" | "diverged A B" | noupstream
    14	  local c a b
    15	  c="$(git -C "$1" rev-list --left-right --count 'HEAD...@{u}' 2>/dev/null)" || { echo noupstream; return; }
    16	  [ -n "$c" ] || { echo noupstream; return; }
    17	  a="${c%%[[:space:]]*}"; b="${c##*[[:space:]]}"
    18	  if   [ "$a" -eq 0 ] && [ "$b" -eq 0 ]; then echo "sync"
    19	  elif [ "$a" -gt 0 ] && [ "$b" -gt 0 ]; then echo "diverged $a $b"
    20	  elif [ "$b" -gt 0 ];                   then echo "behind $b"
    21	  else                                        echo "ahead $a"; fi
    22	}
    23	
    24	if [ "${1:-}" = "--selftest" ]; then
    25	  # Falsification test: build real repos in each state, demand the RIGHT answer.
    26	  # Inverting sync_state must turn these red — that is what makes it a test.
    27	  t="$(mktemp -d)" || t=""
    28	  { [ -n "$t" ] && [ -d "$t" ]; } || { echo "✗ selftest: mktemp -d failed — refusing to run with an empty \$t" >&2; exit 2; }
    29	  trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT; fails=0
    30	  q(){ git -C "$1" "${@:2}" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
    31	  git init -q --bare "$t/origin.git"
    32	  git clone -q "$t/origin.git" "$t/wc" 2>/dev/null
    33	  q "$t/wc" config user.email t@t; q "$t/wc" config user.name t
    34	  seed(){ echo "$1" > "$t/wc/f"; q "$t/wc" add f; q "$t/wc" commit -m "$1"; }
    35	  seed base; q "$t/wc" push -u origin HEAD
    36	  expect(){ got="$(sync_state "${3:-$t/wc}")"
    37	    if [ "$got" = "$2" ]; then printf "  ✓ %-26s → %s\n" "$1" "$got"
    38	    else printf "  ✗ %-26s → got '%s', want '%s'\n" "$1" "$got" "$2"; fails=$((fails+1)); fi; }
    39	
    40	  expect "clean clone"        "sync"
    41	  seed ahead1; seed ahead2
    42	  expect "2 unpushed commits" "ahead 2"           # the case that printed "git pull"
    43	  q "$t/wc" push origin HEAD
    44	  expect "after push"         "sync"
    45	  git clone -q "$t/origin.git" "$t/other"; q "$t/other" config user.email t@t; q "$t/other" config user.name t
    46	  echo remote > "$t/other/g"; q "$t/other" add g; q "$t/other" commit -m remote; q "$t/other" push origin HEAD
    47	  q "$t/wc" fetch origin
    48	  expect "1 commit on remote" "behind 1"
    49	  seed local1
    50	  expect "both sides moved"   "diverged 1 1"
    51	  git init -q "$t/noup"; q "$t/noup" config user.email t@t; q "$t/noup" config user.name t
    52	  echo x > "$t/noup/f"; q "$t/noup" add f; q "$t/noup" commit -m x
    53	  expect "no upstream"        "noupstream"  "$t/noup"
    54	
    55	  [ "$fails" -eq 0 ] && { echo "◆ selftest PASS (6/6)"; exit 0; } || { echo "◆ selftest FAIL ($fails)"; exit 1; }
    56	fi
    57	
    58	echo "◆ AI Review Jury — health check"
    59	
    60	# 1. panel resolves (default or panel.conf), and to which models
    61	panel="$(OPENROUTER_API_KEY=x bash "$HERE/jury.sh" --commit HEAD 2>&1 | grep -oE 'reviewing in parallel — .*' | sed 's/reviewing in parallel — //')"
    62	[ -n "$panel" ] && say "✓" "panel: $panel" || say "✗" "panel did not resolve (jury.sh broken?)"
    63	
    64	# 2. OpenRouter key reachable (env, or the note tells you where yours lives)
    65	# Every runner self-provisions via ork, so "not in this shell" is NOT a problem —
    66	# reporting it as one made the check exit 1 while the jury was fully operational.
    67	if [ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ]; then say "✓" "OPENROUTER_API_KEY present in env"
    68	elif [ -n "$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)" ]; then say "✓" "key self-provisions via ork (not in env, but every runner resolves it)"
    69	else say "✗" "no OPENROUTER_API_KEY in env and ork could not supply one — /jury will fail"; fi
    70	
    71	# 3. slash command / skill installed
    72	insts=""; [ -f "$HOME/.claude/commands/jury.md" ] && insts+="/jury "; [ -d "$HOME/.claude/skills/ai-review-jury" ] && insts+="skill "
    73	[ -n "$insts" ] && say "✓" "installed: ${insts}" || say "○" "no /jury command or skill in ~/.claude (install per the README)"
    74	
    75	# 4. repo live + in sync with origin
    76	if git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    77	  git -C "$HERE" fetch -q origin 2>/dev/null || true
    78	  at="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --short HEAD)"
    79	  # ONE invocation — calling sync_state again inside each branch made the reported
    80	  # state re-entrant: a second call that failed would downgrade a real DIVERGED to
    81	  # "can't compare" (jury P1, 2026-07-27).
    82	  set -- $(sync_state "$HERE")
    83	  case "${1:-}" in
    84	    sync)     say "✓" "repo LIVE + in sync @ $at" ;;
    85	    diverged) say "✗" "repo DIVERGED @ $at — $2 ahead, $3 behind (rebase)" ;;
    86	    behind)   say "✗" "repo BEHIND origin @ $at — $2 behind (git pull)" ;;
    87	    ahead)    say "○" "repo AHEAD @ $at — $2 unpushed; review WHAT is in them before pushing (this remote is public)" ;;
    88	    *)        say "○" "no upstream branch — can't compare" ;;
    89	  esac
    90	else
    91	  say "○" "not a git checkout (can't verify live)"
    92	fi
    93	
    94	# 5. the private-file push guard is ACTIVE, not merely present in the tree.
    95	# Git never auto-runs hooks from a clone (deliberate, and no repo content can change
    96	# it), so an uninstalled guard is the default state. Report it every session rather
    97	# than assuming it — a guard nobody installed is not a guard. (review-gate P1, 07-27)
    98	hp="$(git -C "$HERE" config core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null)"
    99	case "${hp:-}" in
   100	  /*) guard="$hp/pre-push" ;;                      # absolute hooksPath
   101	  "") guard="$HERE/.git/hooks/pre-push" ;;
   102	  *)  guard="$HERE/$hp/pre-push" ;;
   103	esac
   104	# PROBE it, don't just stat it. Testing `-x` certifies any executable — including a
   105	# stub containing `exit 0` — as "the privacy guard" (review-gate P2, 07-27). Feed it
   106	# an unresolvable range: a working guard fails CLOSED (non-zero), a stub returns 0.
   107	# BOTH directions: an `exit 1` stub blocks the bogus range too, and would be
   108	# certified while breaking every legitimate push (review-gate P2, 07-27).
   109	# A real guard REFUSES an unresolvable range and PERMITS a branch deletion.
   110	_feed(){ printf '%s %s %s %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" | "$guard" origin probe >/dev/null 2>&1; }
   111	Z0=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
   112	probe_blocks(){ ! _feed refs/heads/p 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 refs/heads/p 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222; }
   113	probe_permits(){ _feed "(delete)" "$Z0" refs/heads/p 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333; }
   114	if [ -x "$guard" ] && probe_blocks && probe_permits; then
   115	  say "✓" "private-file push guard active AND blocking (probed, not just present)"
   116	elif [ -x "$guard" ]; then
   117	  say "✗" "a pre-push hook exists but does NOT block — it is not this guard (inert stub?)"
   118	else
   119	  say "✗" "push guard NOT installed — private files can reach this PUBLIC remote. Fix: git -C $HERE config core.hooksPath hooks"
   120	fi
   121	
   122	# 6. panel freshness (jury-tune stamps this)
   123	if [ -f "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" ]; then
   124	  d=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(cat "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ) / 86400 ))
   125	  [ "$d" -lt 7 ] && say "✓" "panel tuned ${d}d ago (fresh)" || say "○" "panel ${d}d old — run jury-tune to re-benchmark"
   126	else
   127	  say "○" "never tuned — run jury-tune to establish a baseline"
   128	fi
   129	
   130	echo "◆ $ok ok, $bad problem(s)."
   131	[ "$bad" -eq 0 ]
===== jury.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# jury.sh — a JURY of diverse-lineage models reviews the same diff, in parallel.
     3	#
     4	# One model's blind spots are systematic — a different training lineage has
     5	# *different* blind spots, so a panel of diverse models catches bugs any single
     6	# one misses. (This is the same reason two human reviewers beat one.) The catch:
     7	# a model only helps if it's actually strong on YOUR code — a leaderboard rank
     8	# doesn't transfer. Use ./bench to find out which models earn a seat.
     9	#
    10	# Usage (from inside a git repo): same args as juror.sh, forwarded verbatim.
    11	#   jury.sh                      # branch vs origin/main
    12	#   jury.sh --commit <sha>
    13	#   jury.sh --uncommitted "focus on the auth changes"
    14	#
    15	# Env:
    16	#   OPENROUTER_API_KEY   required
    17	#   MODELS               comma-separated OpenRouter slugs. Default = the two models that
    18	#                        actually EARNED their seat in a 10-diff benchmark (see ./bench and
    19	#                        the RESULTS): glm-5.2 (6/7 real bugs) + minimax-m3 (3/7, and it
    20	#                        caught the one GLM missed) — together 7/7, fast, complementary.
    21	#                        We tested deepseek-v4-pro (3/7 but slow+flaky, 0 unique) and
    22	#                        claude-sonnet-4.5 (1/7, 19 false positives) as a 3rd seat: neither
    23	#                        added signal, both added noise, so the panel stays at two. Running
    24	#                        inside Claude Code, your own session is the effective 3rd reviewer.
    25	#                        Re-benchmark when new models drop; distinct LINEAGES > count.
    26	set -euo pipefail
    27	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    28	# Self-updating panel: `jury-tune` benchmarks new OpenRouter models and writes the
    29	# winners to panel.conf (one line of comma-separated slugs). Falls back to the
    30	# benchmarked default. Env MODELS overrides everything.
    31	PANEL_DEFAULT="z-ai/glm-5.2,minimax/minimax-m3"
    32	PANEL_FILE=""
    33	[ -f "$HERE/panel.conf" ] && PANEL_FILE="$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$HERE/panel.conf" | head -1 | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    34	MODELS="${MODELS:-${PANEL_FILE:-$PANEL_DEFAULT}}"
    35	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    36	[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    37	
    38	# Staleness nudge: new models ship constantly and a leaderboard rank doesn't transfer,
    39	# so prompt a re-benchmark after a week of use. jury-tune stamps .jury-last-tuned.
    40	if [ -f "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" ]; then
    41	  _age=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(cat "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ) / 86400 ))
    42	  [ "$_age" -ge 7 ] && echo "◆ ⚠ Panel is ${_age}d old — new models may have shipped. Re-benchmark + self-update: run jury-tune (or /jury-tune)." >&2
    43	fi
    44	
    45	IFS=',' read -ra LIST <<< "$MODELS"
    46	echo "◆ AI Review Jury: ${#LIST[@]} models reviewing in parallel — ${MODELS}" >&2
    47	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
    48	pids=()
    49	for m in "${LIST[@]}"; do
    50	  safe="${m//\//_}"
    51	  ( MODEL="$m" bash "$HERE/juror.sh" "$@" > "$TMP/$safe.txt" 2>"$TMP/$safe.err" || true ) &
    52	  pids+=($!)
    53	done
    54	for p in "${pids[@]}"; do wait "$p"; done
    55	
    56	for m in "${LIST[@]}"; do
    57	  safe="${m//\//_}"
    58	  echo
    59	  echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
    60	  echo "  $m"
    61	  echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
    62	  cat "$TMP/$safe.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo "(no output)"
    63	done
    64	rm -rf "$TMP"
    65	echo
    66	echo "◆ Panel done. Triage each finding against the code — a claim is a lead, not a verdict." >&2
===== panel.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# panel.sh — a PANEL of diverse-lineage models critiques any text, in parallel.
     3	#
     4	# Same thesis as jury.sh (diverse lineages = non-overlapping blind spots), but
     5	# generalized past git diffs: feed it an idea, a plan, marketing copy, or a UI
     6	# spec and get N independent critiques to triage. The panel are CRITICS, never
     7	# executors — treat every finding as a lead, not a verdict.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   panel.sh --preset idea  pitch.md            # critique a business/product idea
    11	#   panel.sh --preset plan  plan.md "focus on rollback"
    12	#   panel.sh --preset copy  lander-copy.md
    13	#   panel.sh --preset design spec.md            # text spec critique (NOT rendered UI —
    14	#                                               #   use /design-verify for screenshots)
    15	#   cat idea.md | panel.sh --preset idea -      # read from stdin
    16	#
    17	# Env:
    18	#   OPENROUTER_API_KEY  required
    19	#   MODELS              override the panel (comma-separated OpenRouter slugs).
    20	#                       Default: per-preset winners in panels.conf (written by the
    21	#                       panel benchmark), falling back to the code-review pair.
    22	#   PANEL_TIMEOUT       per-model seconds (default 240)
    23	#   MAX_CHARS           truncate input (default 60000)
    24	set -euo pipefail
    25	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    26	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    27	[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    28	
    29	PRESET="generic"
    30	[ "${1:-}" = "--preset" ] && { PRESET="$2"; shift 2; }
    31	SRC="${1:--}"; FOCUS="${2:-}"
    32	if [ "$SRC" = "-" ]; then CONTENT="$(cat)"; else CONTENT="$(cat "$SRC")"; fi
    33	[ -n "$CONTENT" ] || { echo "✗ empty input" >&2; exit 1; }
    34	
    35	# One prompt per preset. Same shape as the code juror: concrete findings, severity
    36	# tags, cite the claim, and an explicit "if it's sound, say so" to measure restraint.
    37	TAIL="Tag each finding P1 (fatal/blocking) / P2 (serious) / P3 (minor). For each, QUOTE or cite the specific claim/section and give one line of concrete evidence — a specific scenario where it fails or misleads. Vague 'this might have issues' does not count. If the input is fundamentally sound, say so plainly. Be precise — false positives waste the reader's time."
    38	case "$PRESET" in
    39	  idea)   ROLE="You are a ruthless startup advisor reviewing a business/product idea. Find CONCRETE flaws only: unit-economics that don't add up (do the arithmetic), internal contradictions, regulatory/legal blockers, market-size math errors, unaddressed cold-start or channel-conflict problems, moats that aren't moats.";;
    40	  plan)   ROLE="You are a senior staff engineer reviewing an implementation/rollout plan. Find CONCRETE flaws only: wrong step ordering, missing rollback for risky steps, race conditions between steps, irreversible actions before verification, dependencies on things not yet deployed, environment/config steps applied to only one env, timezone/cutoff errors.";;
    41	  copy)   ROLE="You are a conversion copywriter and compliance reviewer critiquing marketing copy. Find CONCRETE flaws only: claims that contradict each other, legally risky unsubstantiated claims (guarantees, superlatives), CTA/audience mismatches, spam/GDPR problems in outbound copy, urgency or social proof that is internally inconsistent, feature-dumps where the reader needs benefits.";;
    42	  design) ROLE="You are a senior product designer and accessibility reviewer critiquing a UI spec. Find CONCRETE flaws only: contrast/readability failures, unlabeled or icon-only controls, missing responsive behavior for stated viewports, destructive actions without confirmation, cognitive overload (too many options/fields/steps), state communicated by color alone, missing progress/feedback affordances.";;
    43	  *)      ROLE="You are a rigorous expert reviewer. Find CONCRETE flaws in the following document: internal contradictions, arithmetic errors, unsupported claims, missing critical steps or considerations.";;
    44	esac
    45	PROMPT="$ROLE $TAIL${FOCUS:+ Focus: $FOCUS}"
    46	
    47	# Staleness nudge (mirrors jury.sh): preset seats are empirical and models ship weekly.
    48	# IMPORTANT for re-tunes: the published panel-bench fixtures may be in newer models'
    49	# training data — always write FRESH planted-flaw fixtures (see panel-bench/ANSWER_KEY.md
    50	# for the pattern); reusing published ones inflates challenger scores.
    51	if [ -f "$HERE/.panel-last-tuned" ]; then
    52	  _age=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(cat "$HERE/.panel-last-tuned" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ) / 86400 ))
    53	  [ "$_age" -ge 30 ] && echo "◆ ⚠ Panel seats are ${_age}d old — re-benchmark with FRESH fixtures (panel-bench/, then update panels.conf + stamp .panel-last-tuned)." >&2
    54	fi
    55	
    56	# Panel selection: MODELS env > panels.conf per-preset line > code-review default.
    57	PANEL_DEFAULT="z-ai/glm-5.2,minimax/minimax-m3"
    58	CONF=""
    59	[ -f "$HERE/panels.conf" ] && CONF="$(grep -E "^${PRESET}=" "$HERE/panels.conf" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    60	MODELS="${MODELS:-${CONF:-$PANEL_DEFAULT}}"
    61	
    62	run_one() {
    63	  local model="$1" prompt_override="${2:-$PROMPT}"
    64	  local req
    65	  req=$(python3 -c '
    66	import json,sys
    67	prompt, content, model, mx = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4])
    68	print(json.dumps({
    69	  "model": model,
    70	  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt + "\n\n---\n\n" + content[:mx]}],
    71	  "temperature": 0,
    72	}))' "$prompt_override" "$CONTENT" "$model" "${MAX_CHARS:-60000}")
    73	  curl -s -m "${PANEL_TIMEOUT:-240}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
    74	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    75	    -H "X-Title: AI Review Panel" \
    76	    -d "$req" | python3 -c '
    77	import json,sys
    78	raw = sys.stdin.read()
    79	try: d = json.loads(raw)
    80	except Exception as e:
    81	  print("✗ non-JSON response ("+str(e)+"); first 300 chars:"); print(raw[:300]); sys.exit(1)
    82	if isinstance(d, dict) and d.get("error"):
    83	  print("✗ model error:", d["error"]); sys.exit(1)
    84	try:
    85	  m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
    86	  txt = m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning_content") or m.get("reasoning") or ""
    87	except Exception:
    88	  print("✗ unexpected response shape; first 300 chars:"); print(raw[:300]); sys.exit(1)
    89	print(txt if txt else "(empty response)")'
    90	}
    91	
    92	# OpenRouter drops ~4% of calls (truncated/non-JSON); one retry recovered 7/7 failures
    93	# in the 2026-07-05 benchmark, so retry once before reporting an error.
    94	run_with_retry() {
    95	  local m="$1" out="$2" prompt_override="${3:-$PROMPT}"
    96	  run_one "$m" "$prompt_override" > "$out" 2>&1 || true
    97	  if [ ! -s "$out" ] || grep -q '^✗' "$out"; then
    98	    echo "◆ retrying $m (bad response)" >&2
    99	    run_one "$m" "$prompt_override" > "$out" 2>&1 || true
   100	  fi
   101	}
   102	
   103	IFS=',' read -ra LIST <<< "$MODELS"
   104	echo "◆ AI Panel [$PRESET]: ${#LIST[@]} models critiquing in parallel — ${MODELS}" >&2
   105	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
   106	for m in "${LIST[@]}"; do
   107	  ( run_with_retry "$m" "$TMP/${m//\//_}.txt" ) &
   108	done
   109	wait
   110	for m in "${LIST[@]}"; do
   111	  echo; echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
   112	  echo "  $m"
   113	  echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
   114	  cat "$TMP/${m//\//_}.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo "(no output)"
   115	done
   116	
   117	# COUNCIL=1 — anonymized cross-examination round (llm-council Stage 2, adopted 2026-07-07).
   118	# Each panelist reviews the OTHERS' findings blind (Reviewer A/B/…) and must CONFIRM or
   119	# REFUTE each with concrete evidence. Kills false positives before the human triage and
   120	# surfaces which disagreements deserve the hardest look. Doubles cost (still pennies).
   121	if [ "${COUNCIL:-0}" = "1" ] && [ "${#LIST[@]}" -ge 2 ]; then
   122	  echo "◆ Council round: anonymized cross-examination" >&2
   123	  for m in "${LIST[@]}"; do
   124	    others=""; letter=A
   125	    for o in "${LIST[@]}"; do
   126	      [ "$o" = "$m" ] && continue
   127	      others="${others}───── Reviewer ${letter} (identity hidden) ─────
   128	$(cat "$TMP/${o//\//_}.txt" 2>/dev/null)
   129	
   130	"
   131	      letter=$(printf '%s' "$letter" | tr 'A-Y' 'B-Z')
   132	    done
   133	    CROSS="You are cross-examining another reviewer's findings on the SAME document you just reviewed (the document follows after the findings). For EACH of their findings, output one line: CONFIRM — <the corroborating evidence> or REFUTE — <the concrete counter-evidence>. Do not be polite; a wrong CONFIRM wastes the maintainer's time. Finish with two lines: (1) their single most important finding, (2) anything real they caught that you missed.
   134	
   135	${others}The original document for reference:"
   136	    ( run_with_retry "$m" "$TMP/${m//\//_}.cross.txt" "$CROSS" ) &
   137	  done
   138	  wait
   139	  for m in "${LIST[@]}"; do
   140	    echo; echo "──────────── cross-examination by $m ────────────"
   141	    cat "$TMP/${m//\//_}.cross.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo "(no output)"
   142	  done
   143	fi
   144	echo
   145	echo "◆ Panel done. Triage each finding — a claim is a lead, not a verdict." >&2
===== tune-collect.sh =====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# tune-collect.sh — gather candidate reviews for a self-update benchmark.
     3	#
     4	# Fetches the live OpenRouter model list, picks the current panel (incumbents) plus
     5	# fresh CHALLENGERS (models that appeared since the last tune), and runs each over
     6	# your recent diffs. It does NOT judge or decide — the /jury-tune skill reads these
     7	# reviews, verifies each finding against the code, ranks by VERIFIED-real bugs vs
     8	# false positives, and rewrites panel.conf. This split keeps the judgment where the
     9	# code context is (the Claude session), same as /jury itself.
    10	#
    11	# Env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (req). OUT (./jury-tune-run). N_DIFFS (8). N_CHALLENGERS (5).
    12	#      CHALLENGERS="a,b,c" to pick them yourself. INCUMBENTS overrides the current panel.
    13	set -uo pipefail
    14	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    15	OUT="${OUT:-./jury-tune-run}"
    16	N_DIFFS="${N_DIFFS:-8}"
    17	N_CHALLENGERS="${N_CHALLENGERS:-5}"
    18	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    19	[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    20	git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "✗ run inside the repo to benchmark against" >&2; exit 1; }
    21	mkdir -p "$OUT/reviews"
    22	
    23	PANEL_DEFAULT="z-ai/glm-5.2,minimax/minimax-m3"
    24	[ -f "$HERE/panel.conf" ] && PANEL_DEFAULT="$(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*(#|$)' "$HERE/panel.conf" | head -1 | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    25	INCUMBENTS="${INCUMBENTS:-$PANEL_DEFAULT}"
    26	SINCE=0; [ -f "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" ] && SINCE="$(cat "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    27	
    28	# Challengers: plausible reviewers (no free/media tiers, ≥32k ctx) that appeared
    29	# since the last tune, newest first, ONE per lineage for diversity, capped.
    30	if [ -n "${CHALLENGERS:-}" ]; then
    31	  CH="$CHALLENGERS"
    32	else
    33	  CH="$(curl -s -m 30 https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models | python3 -c '
    34	import json,sys
    35	since=int(sys.argv[1]); n=int(sys.argv[2]); inc=set(x for x in sys.argv[3].split(",") if x)
    36	try: data=json.load(sys.stdin).get("data",[])
    37	except Exception: print(""); sys.exit()
    38	bad=("free","image","vision","tts","whisper","embed","audio","guard","ocr","dall")
    39	def ok(m):
    40	    i=m.get("id","").lower()
    41	    if m.get("id") in inc: return False           # already on the panel
    42	    if any(b in i for b in bad): return False
    43	    if (m.get("context_length") or 0) < 32000: return False
    44	    if since and (m.get("created") or 0) <= since: return False
    45	    return True
    46	c=sorted([m for m in data if ok(m)], key=lambda m: -(m.get("created") or 0))
    47	seen=set(); out=[]
    48	for m in c:
    49	    lin=m["id"].split("/")[0]
    50	    if lin in seen: continue
    51	    seen.add(lin); out.append(m["id"])
    52	    if len(out)>=n: break
    53	print(",".join(out))
    54	' "$SINCE" "$N_CHALLENGERS" "$INCUMBENTS")"
    55	fi
    56	
    57	echo "◆ incumbents:  $INCUMBENTS" >&2
    58	echo "◆ challengers: ${CH:-(none new since last tune — nothing to test)}" >&2
    59	ALL="$INCUMBENTS${CH:+,$CH}"
    60	
    61	mapfile -t COMMITS < <(git log --no-merges -"$N_DIFFS" --format="%h")
    62	[ "${#COMMITS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "✗ no commits to benchmark" >&2; exit 1; }
    63	
    64	run(){ local sha="$1" m="$2"; local s="${m//\//_}"
    65	  timeout 300 env MODEL="$m" bash "$HERE/juror.sh" --commit "$sha" > "$OUT/reviews/${sha}__${s}.txt" 2>&1 || echo "(error/timeout)" >> "$OUT/reviews/${sha}__${s}.txt"
    66	  echo "  ✓ $sha $m"; }
    67	export -f run; export HERE OUT
    68	echo "◆ running $(echo "$ALL" | tr ',' '\n' | wc -l) models × ${#COMMITS[@]} diffs…" >&2
    69	IFS=',' read -ra MLIST <<< "$ALL"
    70	# -n 2: sha + model as two argv tokens (the old -I{} passed the pair as ONE
    71	# arg → run() saw m="" and built "sha model__.txt" paths that never existed).
    72	{ for sha in "${COMMITS[@]}"; do for m in "${MLIST[@]}"; do echo "$sha $m"; done; done; } | xargs -P 6 -n 2 bash -c 'run "$1" "$2"' _
    73	
    74	printf "incumbents=%s\nchallengers=%s\ndiffs=%s\n" "$INCUMBENTS" "${CH:-none}" "${COMMITS[*]}" > "$OUT/candidates.txt"
    75	echo "◆ collected → $OUT/reviews/ ($(ls "$OUT/reviews" | wc -l) reviews). Next: /jury-tune judges + rewrites panel.conf." >&2

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# idea-panel.sh — the divergence-map front end for an idea/plan.
     3	#
     4	# Not "N models critique in parallel" (that's panel.sh). This surfaces WHERE
     5	# diverse perspectives DISAGREE — because disagreement is the signal worth
     6	# researching. Pipeline:
     7	#   0. LEDGER FIRST — brain-search the idea's terms; a prior verdict beats a
     8	#      fresh debate (the 2026-07-24 lesson: the vault already had the answer).
     9	#   1. Three ROLE-diverse, LINEAGE-diverse perspectives: advocate / skeptic /
    10	#      researcher (role framing changes output — proven in the bake-off).
    11	#   2. Synthesis into a DIVERGENCE MAP: consensus | disagreements+crux | unknowns.
    12	#   3. Append to the idea-ledger for later preference/reliability learning.
    13	#
    14	# Usage:  idea-panel.sh idea.md ["optional focus"]
    15	#         echo "my idea..." | idea-panel.sh -
    16	#
    17	# Env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (req). MODELS_ADVOCATE/SKEPTIC/RESEARCHER/SYNTH override roles.
    18	set -euo pipefail
    19	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

    22	
    23	SRC="${1:--}"; FOCUS="${2:-}"

    26	MAX=${MAX_CHARS:-40000}; CONTENT="${CONTENT:0:$MAX}"
    27	
    28	# Role→model. Candidates (deepseek-v4-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite) sit in the
    29	# generative roles so each run measures their PLANNING signal; the proven
    30	# critic/synth models (minimax, glm) hold the judgement seats.
    31	M_ADV="${MODELS_ADVOCATE:-deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash}"
    32	M_SKEP="${MODELS_SKEPTIC:-minimax/minimax-m3}"
    33	M_RES="${MODELS_RESEARCHER:-google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite}"
    34	M_SYNTH="${MODELS_SYNTH:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
    35	
    36	call() { # model, prompt  ->  text
    37	  local model="$1" prompt="$2" req

    40	print(json.dumps({"model":sys.argv[3],"temperature":0,
    41	  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":sys.argv[1]+"\n\n--- IDEA ---\n"+sys.argv[2]}]}))' \
    42	    "$prompt" "$CONTENT" "$model")

    44	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    45	    -H "X-Title: idea-panel" -d "$req" | python3 -c '
    46	import json,sys
    47	raw=sys.stdin.read()
    48	try: d=json.loads(raw)
    49	except Exception: print("(non-JSON response)"); sys.exit(1)
    50	if isinstance(d,dict) and d.get("error"): print("(model error:",d["error"],")"); sys.exit(1)
    51	try:
    52	  m=d["choices"][0]["message"]; body=m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning")

    55	except Exception: print("(bad shape:",raw[:200],")"); sys.exit(1)'

    58	FOCUS_LINE="${FOCUS:+ The user asks you to focus on: $FOCUS.}"

    60	P_SKEP="You are a SKEPTIC. You think this idea is likely flawed. Find the CONCRETE reasons it fails: unit-economics that don't add up (do the math), internal contradictions, hidden costs, false assumptions, why it won't work as imagined, simpler things that already solve it. No vague doubts — specific failure modes only.$FOCUS_LINE"

Identify what is UNKNOWN: the load-bearing ASSUMPTIONS that need checking, the QUESTIONS whose answers would flip the verdict, and for each, HOW to find the answer (what to test, measure, or look up). Rank by how much the answer would change the decision.$FOCUS_LINE"
    62	
    63	echo "◆ idea-panel: ledger → advocate($M_ADV) · skeptic($M_SKEP) · researcher($M_RES) → divergence map" >&2
    64	
    65	# ── 0. LEDGER FIRST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    66	echo "═══ 0 · PRIOR KNOWLEDGE (brain-search) ═══"
    67	TERMS=$(python3 -c '
    68	import re,sys,collections
    69	stop=set("this that with have from your will they them then than into over about which what when where would could should being your yours idea plan system user users".split())
    70	w=[x.lower() for x in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]{5,}", sys.stdin.read())]
    71	c=collections.Counter(x for x in w if x not in stop)

    73	echo "  terms: $TERMS"

    77	PRIOR_DECISIONS="$(grep -A2 '^### DECISION' "$HERE/idea-ledger.md" 2>/dev/null | tail -40 || true)"

    79	
    80	# ── 1. THREE ROLE-DIVERSE PERSPECTIVES (parallel) ────────────────────────────
    81	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
    82	( call "$M_ADV"  "$P_ADV"  > "$TMP/adv"  2>&1 || touch "$TMP/adv.fail"  ) &
    83	( call "$M_SKEP" "$P_SKEP" > "$TMP/skep" 2>&1 || touch "$TMP/skep.fail" ) &
    84	( call "$M_RES"  "$P_RES"  > "$TMP/res"  2>&1 || touch "$TMP/res.fail"  ) &
    85	wait
    86	echo; echo "═══ 1 · PERSPECTIVES ═══"
    87	for r in "ADVOCATE:$M_ADV:adv" "SKEPTIC:$M_SKEP:skep" "RESEARCHER:$M_RES:res"; do
    88	  IFS=: read -r label model file <<<"$r"
    89	  echo; echo "── $label ($model) ──"; cat "$TMP/$file"
    90	done
    91	
    92	# A map synthesized from error strings is indistinguishable from a real one once
    93	# it is in the ledger. If any perspective failed, stop here (review-gate P2, 07-27).
    94	if compgen -G "$TMP/*.fail" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    95	  echo >&2; echo "✗ perspective(s) FAILED above — refusing to synthesize a divergence map" >&2
    96	  echo "  from error text, and NOT appending to the ledger." >&2; exit 1
    97	fi
    98	
    99	# ── 2. DIVERGENCE MAP ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   100	# %s not %b: model output is untrusted and %b would interpret its backslash
   101	# escapes — a returned "\\c" truncates the bundle silently. (review-gate P2, 07-27)
   102	BUNDLE="$(printf 'ADVOCATE said:\n%s\n\nSKEPTIC said:\n%s\n\nRESEARCHER said:\n%s\n' \

   104	P_SYNTH="Below are three perspectives (advocate/skeptic/researcher) on the same idea. Produce a DIVERGENCE MAP, nothing else:
   105	1. CONSENSUS — points all three implicitly agree on (the safe ground).
   106	2. DISAGREEMENTS — where they genuinely conflict. For EACH, state the CRUX: the single question whose answer decides who is right.
   107	3. TOP UNKNOWNS TO RESEARCH — ranked by how much resolving them would change the decision; name the concrete check for each.
   108	Be terse and concrete. Do not re-argue the idea; map the structure of the disagreement.${PRIOR_DECISIONS:+
   109	
   110	The user has made these PRIOR DECISIONS on related ideas (their taste signal) — weight the map toward what they have valued, and FLAG if this idea repeats or contradicts a past decision:
   111	$PRIOR_DECISIONS}"

   114	
   115	$P_SYNTH") || {
   116	  echo "✗ synthesis failed — NOT appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
   117	echo "$MAP"

   119	# ── 3. LEDGER APPEND (capture for later learning) ────────────────────────────
   120	LEDGER="$HERE/idea-ledger.md"
