   124	echo; echo "◆ appended to $LEDGER (add your pick + why later → feeds preference learning)" >&2
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# jury-check.sh — 5-second health check: is the jury wired, current, and live?
     3	# Run at the start of a session to confirm /jury is set up within normal parameters.
     4	set -uo pipefail
     5	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
     6	ok=0; bad=0
     7	say(){ printf "  %s %s\n" "$1" "$2"; [ "$1" = "✓" ] && ok=$((ok+1)) || bad=$((bad+1)); }
     8	
     9	# ONE definition, used by the check AND by --selftest, so they cannot drift.
    10	# SHA equality (the original) cannot tell ahead from behind: it printed "BEHIND —
    11	# git pull" at a checkout sitting on unpushed commits, which is the only direction
    12	# that can publish something. Fixtures below prove all four states.
    13	sync_state(){ # repo -> sync | "ahead N" | "behind N" | "diverged A B" | noupstream
    14	  local c a b
    15	  c="$(git -C "$1" rev-list --left-right --count 'HEAD...@{u}' 2>/dev/null)" || { echo noupstream; return; }
    16	  [ -n "$c" ] || { echo noupstream; return; }
    17	  a="${c%%[[:space:]]*}"; b="${c##*[[:space:]]}"
    18	  if   [ "$a" -eq 0 ] && [ "$b" -eq 0 ]; then echo "sync"
    19	  elif [ "$a" -gt 0 ] && [ "$b" -gt 0 ]; then echo "diverged $a $b"
    20	  elif [ "$b" -gt 0 ];                   then echo "behind $b"
    21	  else                                        echo "ahead $a"; fi
    22	}
    23	
    24	if [ "${1:-}" = "--selftest" ]; then
    25	  # Falsification test: build real repos in each state, demand the RIGHT answer.
    26	  # Inverting sync_state must turn these red — that is what makes it a test.
    27	  t="$(mktemp -d)" || t=""
    28	  { [ -n "$t" ] && [ -d "$t" ]; } || { echo "✗ selftest: mktemp -d failed — refusing to run with an empty \$t" >&2; exit 2; }
    29	  trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT; fails=0
    30	  q(){ git -C "$1" "${@:2}" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
    31	  git init -q --bare "$t/origin.git"
    32	  git clone -q "$t/origin.git" "$t/wc" 2>/dev/null
    33	  q "$t/wc" config user.email t@t; q "$t/wc" config user.name t
    34	  seed(){ echo "$1" > "$t/wc/f"; q "$t/wc" add f; q "$t/wc" commit -m "$1"; }
    35	  seed base; q "$t/wc" push -u origin HEAD
    36	  expect(){ got="$(sync_state "${3:-$t/wc}")"
    37	    if [ "$got" = "$2" ]; then printf "  ✓ %-26s → %s\n" "$1" "$got"
    38	    else printf "  ✗ %-26s → got '%s', want '%s'\n" "$1" "$got" "$2"; fails=$((fails+1)); fi; }
    39	
    40	  expect "clean clone"        "sync"
    41	  seed ahead1; seed ahead2
    42	  expect "2 unpushed commits" "ahead 2"           # the case that printed "git pull"
    43	  q "$t/wc" push origin HEAD
    44	  expect "after push"         "sync"
    45	  git clone -q "$t/origin.git" "$t/other"; q "$t/other" config user.email t@t; q "$t/other" config user.name t
    46	  echo remote > "$t/other/g"; q "$t/other" add g; q "$t/other" commit -m remote; q "$t/other" push origin HEAD
    47	  q "$t/wc" fetch origin
    48	  expect "1 commit on remote" "behind 1"
    49	  seed local1
    50	  expect "both sides moved"   "diverged 1 1"
    51	  git init -q "$t/noup"; q "$t/noup" config user.email t@t; q "$t/noup" config user.name t
    52	  echo x > "$t/noup/f"; q "$t/noup" add f; q "$t/noup" commit -m x
    53	  expect "no upstream"        "noupstream"  "$t/noup"
    54	
    55	  [ "$fails" -eq 0 ] && { echo "◆ selftest PASS (6/6)"; exit 0; } || { echo "◆ selftest FAIL ($fails)"; exit 1; }
    56	fi
    57	
    58	echo "◆ AI Review Jury — health check"
    59	
    60	# 1. panel resolves (default or panel.conf), and to which models
    61	panel="$(OPENROUTER_API_KEY=x bash "$HERE/jury.sh" --commit HEAD 2>&1 | grep -oE 'reviewing in parallel — .*' | sed 's/reviewing in parallel — //')"
    62	[ -n "$panel" ] && say "✓" "panel: $panel" || say "✗" "panel did not resolve (jury.sh broken?)"
    63	
    64	# 2. OpenRouter key reachable (env, or the note tells you where yours lives)
    65	# Every runner self-provisions via ork, so "not in this shell" is NOT a problem —
    66	# reporting it as one made the check exit 1 while the jury was fully operational.
    67	if [ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ]; then say "✓" "OPENROUTER_API_KEY present in env"
    68	elif [ -n "$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)" ]; then say "✓" "key self-provisions via ork (not in env, but every runner resolves it)"
    69	else say "✗" "no OPENROUTER_API_KEY in env and ork could not supply one — /jury will fail"; fi
    70	
    71	# 3. slash command / skill installed
    72	insts=""; [ -f "$HOME/.claude/commands/jury.md" ] && insts+="/jury "; [ -d "$HOME/.claude/skills/ai-review-jury" ] && insts+="skill "
    73	[ -n "$insts" ] && say "✓" "installed: ${insts}" || say "○" "no /jury command or skill in ~/.claude (install per the README)"
    74	
    75	# 4. repo live + in sync with origin
    76	if git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    77	  git -C "$HERE" fetch -q origin 2>/dev/null || true
    78	  at="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --short HEAD)"
    79	  # ONE invocation — calling sync_state again inside each branch made the reported
    80	  # state re-entrant: a second call that failed would downgrade a real DIVERGED to
    81	  # "can't compare" (jury P1, 2026-07-27).
    82	  set -- $(sync_state "$HERE")
    83	  case "${1:-}" in
    84	    sync)     say "✓" "repo LIVE + in sync @ $at" ;;
    85	    diverged) say "✗" "repo DIVERGED @ $at — $2 ahead, $3 behind (rebase)" ;;
    86	    behind)   say "✗" "repo BEHIND origin @ $at — $2 behind (git pull)" ;;
    87	    ahead)    say "○" "repo AHEAD @ $at — $2 unpushed; review WHAT is in them before pushing (this remote is public)" ;;
    88	    *)        say "○" "no upstream branch — can't compare" ;;
    89	  esac
    90	else
    91	  say "○" "not a git checkout (can't verify live)"
    92	fi
    93	
    94	# 5. the private-file push guard is ACTIVE, not merely present in the tree.
    95	# Git never auto-runs hooks from a clone (deliberate, and no repo content can change
    96	# it), so an uninstalled guard is the default state. Report it every session rather
    97	# than assuming it — a guard nobody installed is not a guard. (review-gate P1, 07-27)
    98	hp="$(git -C "$HERE" config core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null)"
    99	case "${hp:-}" in
   100	  /*) guard="$hp/pre-push" ;;                      # absolute hooksPath
   101	  "") guard="$HERE/.git/hooks/pre-push" ;;
   102	  *)  guard="$HERE/$hp/pre-push" ;;
   103	esac
   104	# PROBE it, don't just stat it. Testing `-x` certifies any executable — including a
   105	# stub containing `exit 0` — as "the privacy guard" (review-gate P2, 07-27). Feed it
   106	# an unresolvable range: a working guard fails CLOSED (non-zero), a stub returns 0.
   107	# BOTH directions: an `exit 1` stub blocks the bogus range too, and would be
   108	# certified while breaking every legitimate push (review-gate P2, 07-27).
   109	# A real guard REFUSES an unresolvable range and PERMITS a branch deletion.
   110	_feed(){ printf '%s %s %s %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" | "$guard" origin probe >/dev/null 2>&1; }
   111	Z0=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
   112	probe_blocks(){ ! _feed refs/heads/p 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 refs/heads/p 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222; }
   113	probe_permits(){ _feed "(delete)" "$Z0" refs/heads/p 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333; }
   114	if [ -x "$guard" ] && probe_blocks && probe_permits; then
   115	  say "✓" "private-file push guard active AND blocking (probed, not just present)"
   116	elif [ -x "$guard" ]; then
   117	  say "✗" "a pre-push hook exists but does NOT block — it is not this guard (inert stub?)"
   118	else
   119	  say "✗" "push guard NOT installed — private files can reach this PUBLIC remote. Fix: git -C $HERE config core.hooksPath hooks"
   120	fi
   121	
   122	# 6. panel freshness (jury-tune stamps this)
   123	if [ -f "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" ]; then
   124	  d=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(cat "$HERE/.jury-last-tuned" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ) / 86400 ))
   125	  [ "$d" -lt 7 ] && say "✓" "panel tuned ${d}d ago (fresh)" || say "○" "panel ${d}d old — run jury-tune to re-benchmark"
   126	else
   127	  say "○" "never tuned — run jury-tune to establish a baseline"
   128	fi
   129	
   130	echo "◆ $ok ok, $bad problem(s)."
   131	[ "$bad" -eq 0 ]
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# agentic-juror.sh <worktree> <sha> <outprefix> — one foreign-lineage model reviews a
     3	# commit AGENTICALLY (reads callers/config beyond the diff), Codex-style.
     4	# Harness: headless Claude Code pointed at OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint
     5	# (/api/v1/messages passes tool_use through — probed 2026-07-05). Model: GLM-5.2.
     6	# Read-only: enforced with --disallowedTools (deny beats allow). NOTE (10-commit bench
     7	# lesson): --allowedTools alone does NOT restrict — the worktree inherits the repo's
     8	# .claude/settings.json allow rules, so the model also ran grep/npx/curl. Zero writes
     9	# occurred in 10/10 runs, but always verify the writes_check line in the .meta output.
    10	# Proven in the 2026-07-05 smoke test (2 commits, 25 tool calls, 0 format failures,
    11	# 0 writes, ~$0.21-0.41/review): caught the reduced-motion diffBaseline bug diff-only
    12	# GLM missed, plus a new real argv bug. Known wart: `claude -p` result field comes back
    13	# EMPTY (GLM ends with a thinking block) — read the final text from the session
    14	# transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<worktree-slug>/*.jsonl instead.
    15	# ponytail: 2-run smoke evidence, not a reliability study — promote to a standing lane
    16	# only after a 10-commit bench like the diff-only one.
    17	set -uo pipefail
    18	WT="$1"; SHA="$2"; OUT="$3"
    19	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    20	KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}"
    21	[ -n "$KEY" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    22	
    23	credits() { curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/credits -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin)["data"];print(d["total_credits"]-d["total_usage"])'; }
    24	
    25	BEFORE=$(credits); echo "credits_before=$BEFORE" > "$OUT.meta"
    26	START=$(date +%s)
    27	
    28	PROMPT="You are reviewing commit $SHA in this git repo for CORRECTNESS bugs and security issues only — not style. First run: git show $SHA  to see the diff. Then USE THE REPO: read the full files the diff touches and any callers/config they interact with, to verify each suspicion against the real code beyond the diff hunks. Report each finding as P1 (blocking) / P2 (likely bug) / P3 (minor) with file:line and one concrete failing input/state. If part of the diff is correct, don't invent problems. Finish with a FINDINGS list."
    29	
    30	# CLAUDE_AUTOCAPTURE=1 marks this as pipeline-internal so the session-memory hooks
    31	# skip it (inferred from brain-consolidate.sh's use; unmarked smoke runs each spawned
    32	# a ~$0.12 distill child and polluted the auto notes — verify on next run).
    33	cd "$WT" && CLAUDE_AUTOCAPTURE=1 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api" \
    34	  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="$KEY" \
    35	  ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$KEY" \
    36	  ANTHROPIC_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.2" \
    37	  ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.2" \
    38	  CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 \
    39	  timeout 900 claude -p "$PROMPT" \
    40	    --model "z-ai/glm-5.2" \
    41	    --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob,Bash(git show:*),Bash(git log:*),Bash(git diff:*),Bash(cat:*),Bash(ls:*)" \
    42	    --disallowedTools "Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,Task,Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*),Bash(git push:*),Bash(rm:*),Bash(mv:*),Bash(npm install:*),Bash(npx convex:*)" \
    43	    --max-turns 40 \
    44	    --output-format json > "$OUT.json" 2> "$OUT.err"
    45	RC=$?
    46	
    47	AFTER=$(credits)
    48	{ echo "credits_after=$AFTER"
    49	  echo "exit_code=$RC"
    50	  echo "wall_seconds=$(( $(date +%s) - START ))"
    51	  echo "writes_check=$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain | wc -l) dirty files"
    52	} >> "$OUT.meta"
    53	echo "done $SHA rc=$RC"
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# juror.sh — one AI model reviews a git diff for correctness/security bugs.
     3	#
     4	# Reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the env and sends the diff to one model via
     5	# OpenRouter (any model, one API). Read-only: it prints findings, it never edits
     6	# your code. Triage the findings yourself — treat them as leads, not verdicts.
     7	#
     8	# Usage (run from inside a git repo):
     9	#   juror.sh                     # branch diff vs origin/main (or origin/master)
    10	#   juror.sh --base <ref>        # diff vs an arbitrary base ref
    11	#   juror.sh --commit <sha>      # a single commit
    12	#   juror.sh --uncommitted       # your current uncommitted (tracked) changes
    13	#   juror.sh "<focus note>"      # append a focus instruction to the prompt
    14	#
    15	# Env:
    16	#   OPENROUTER_API_KEY   required
    17	#   MODEL                OpenRouter model slug (default: z-ai/glm-5.2 — it won the
    18	#                        benchmark in ./bench; verify slugs at openrouter.ai/models)
    19	#   MAX_DIFF_CHARS       truncate very large diffs (default 120000)
    20	#   REVIEW_TIMEOUT       per-model seconds (default 280 — high enough for slow
    21	#                        reasoning models like deepseek-v4-pro on a large diff)
    22	set -euo pipefail
    23	
    24	# --help must work without a key or a repo.
    25	case "${1:-}" in -h|--help) grep '^#' "$0" | grep -v '^#!' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;; esac
    26	
    27	MODEL="${MODEL:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
    28	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
    29	KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}"
    30	MAX="${MAX_DIFF_CHARS:-120000}"
    31	[ -n "$KEY" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
    32	git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "✗ not in a git repo" >&2; exit 1; }
    33	
    34	MODE=""; BASE=""; FOCUS=""
    35	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --base) MODE="base"; BASE="$2"; shift 2;;
    38	    --commit) MODE="commit"; BASE="$2"; shift 2;;
    39	    --uncommitted) MODE="uncommitted"; shift;;
    40	    -h|--help) grep '^#' "$0" | grep -v '^#!' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;;
    41	    *) FOCUS="$1"; shift;;
    42	  esac
    43	done
    44	
    45	# Default: diff the branch against its upstream default branch.
    46	if [ -z "$MODE" ]; then
    47	  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
    48	    MODE="uncommitted"
    49	  else
    50	    MODE="base"; BASE="origin/main"
    51	    git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1 || BASE="origin/master"
    52	  fi
    53	fi
    54	
    55	case "$MODE" in
    56	  uncommitted) DIFF=$(git diff HEAD); SCOPE="uncommitted changes";;
    57	  base)        DIFF=$(git diff "$BASE"...HEAD); SCOPE="branch vs $BASE";;
    58	  commit)      DIFF=$(git show "$BASE"); SCOPE="commit $BASE";;
    59	esac
    60	[ -n "$DIFF" ] || { echo "◆ nothing to review ($SCOPE)"; exit 0; }
    61	echo "◆ $MODEL reviewing: $SCOPE ($(printf '%s' "$DIFF" | grep -c '^[+-]') changed lines)" >&2
    62	
    63	PROMPT="You are a senior code reviewer. Review this git diff for CORRECTNESS bugs and security issues only — not style. Tag each finding P1 (blocking correctness) / P2 (likely bug) / P3 (minor), each with file:line and one line of concrete evidence: a specific input or state that produces a wrong output. If the diff is correct, say so plainly. Be precise — false positives waste the maintainer's time.${FOCUS:+ Focus: $FOCUS}"
    64	
    65	# Build the JSON body with python so an arbitrary diff can't break quoting.
    66	REQ=$(python3 -c '
    67	import json,sys
    68	prompt, diff, model, mx = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4])
    69	print(json.dumps({
    70	  "model": model,
    71	  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt + "\n\n```diff\n" + diff[:mx] + "\n```"}],
    72	  "temperature": 0,
    73	}))' "$PROMPT" "$DIFF" "$MODEL" "$MAX")
    74	
    75	# OpenRouter drops ~4% of calls (truncated/non-JSON; measured 2026-07-05, 7/7 recovered
    76	# on one retry) — so try twice before reporting an error.
    77	run_review() {
    78	  curl -s -m "${REVIEW_TIMEOUT:-280}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
    79	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    80	    -H "X-Title: AI Review Jury" \
    81	    -d "$REQ" | python3 -c '
    82	import json,sys
    83	raw = sys.stdin.read()
    84	try:
    85	  d = json.loads(raw)
    86	except Exception as e:
    87	  print("✗ non-JSON response ("+str(e)+"); first 300 chars:"); print(raw[:300]); sys.exit(1)
    88	if isinstance(d, dict) and d.get("error"):
    89	  print("✗ model error:", d["error"]); sys.exit(1)
    90	try:
    91	  m = d["choices"][0]["message"]
    92	  # reasoning models sometimes route the answer via reasoning/reasoning_content
    93	  txt = m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning_content") or m.get("reasoning") or ""
    94	except Exception:
    95	  print("✗ unexpected response shape; first 300 chars:"); print(raw[:300]); sys.exit(1)
    96	print(txt if txt else "(empty response)")'
    97	}
    98	OUT="$(run_review)"
    99	if printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -q '^✗\|^(empty response)$'; then
   100	  echo "◆ retrying $MODEL (bad response)" >&2
   101	  OUT="$(run_review)"
   102	fi
   103	printf '%s\n' "$OUT"
     1	# AI Review Jury
     2	
     3	**A jury of diverse AI models reviews your git diff — and a harness to prove which models actually catch bugs in _your_ codebase.**
     4	
     5	One reviewer, human or model, has systematic blind spots. A reviewer from a *different* lineage has *different* blind spots, so a small panel catches bugs any single one misses — the same reason two human reviewers beat one. The catch nobody tells you: **a public leaderboard rank does not transfer to your code.** The only way to know which models earn a seat on your panel is to run them on your own diffs and check the findings. This repo does both.
     6	
     7	- **`juror.sh`** — one model reviews a diff (any model, via [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai)).
     8	- **`jury.sh`** — a diverse panel reviews the same diff in parallel.
     9	- **`panel.sh`** — the same idea generalized past code: a panel critiques an **idea, plan, marketing copy, or UI spec** (per-preset prompts + per-preset benchmarked seats).
    10	- **`agentic-juror.sh`** — one foreign-lineage model reviews a commit **agentically** (Codex-style: reads callers, runs tests, traces beyond the diff) using Claude Code as the harness via OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint.
    11	- **`bench/`** — run N models over your recent commits, triage the findings against the real code, and get a per-model **precision / recall / unique-bugs** scorecard. **`panel-bench/`** — the same for non-code presets, with planted-flaw fixtures (ground truth by construction).
    12	
    13	It's ~200 lines of bash + python. No service, no daemon, no lock-in. It prints findings; **you** triage them — a claim is a lead, not a verdict.
    14	
    15	## Why (a real result)
    16	
    17	I ran a 3-model panel over 10 recent commits of a production Next.js/Convex codebase and hand-verified every finding against the code. The panel found **7 distinct real bugs**:
    18	
    19	| model | raised | REAL | unique-REAL | false positives | precision | recall |
    20	|-------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
    21	| `z-ai/glm-5.2` | 11 | **6** | **4** | 5 | 55% | **86%** |
    22	| `minimax/minimax-m3` | 10 | 3 | 1 | 7 | 30% | 43% |
    23	| `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` | 2 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0% | 0% |
    24	
    25	Two things that a leaderboard would never have told me:
    26	
    27	1. **The cheap flash-tier model was worse than useless** — it found zero real bugs *and* actively certified a real one as safe (a false negative). A weak model doesn't just add little; it adds noise **and** false confidence.
    28	2. **The panel beat any single reviewer.** On one diff, one top model called the change clean — and a different-lineage model caught a real bug in it. That bug only surfaced *because* the lineages disagreed. That's the entire thesis in one data point.
    29	
    30	`unique-REAL` is the number that matters: real bugs **only** that model caught. That's what a model actually adds to a panel you already have. `false positives` is what it charges you in triage time. Add a model when the first column beats the second.
    31	
    32	> **Default panel.** `jury.sh` defaults to `glm-5.2 + minimax-m3` — the two seats that earned their place in the 10-diff benchmark (86% + 43% recall, 7/7 combined; a deepseek-pro and a sonnet third seat were both auditioned and added noise, not signal). Tuned for running *inside* Claude Code: your session is already a Claude reviewer, so the panel spends its slots on non-Claude lineages. Self-updating: `jury-tune` re-benchmarks challengers and writes winners to `panel.conf`; `MODELS=` overrides everything.
    33	
    34	## Setup
    35	
    36	```bash
    37	git clone <this-repo> && cd AI-Review-Jury
    38	chmod +x juror.sh jury.sh bench/collect.sh
    39	export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...        # from openrouter.ai/keys
    40	```
    41	
    42	Requirements: `bash`, `git`, `python3`, `curl`. That's it.
    43	
    44	## Use
    45	
    46	Run from inside the repo you're reviewing:
    47	
    48	```bash
    49	# one model on your branch's diff vs origin/main
    50	/path/to/AI-Review-Jury/juror.sh
    51	
    52	# the full panel on a specific commit
    53	/path/to/AI-Review-Jury/jury.sh --commit 1a2b3c4
    54	
    55	# panel on uncommitted work, with a focus note
    56	/path/to/AI-Review-Jury/jury.sh --uncommitted "focus on the auth and payment changes"
    57	```
    58	
    59	Pick your own panel — distinct **lineages** matter more than count (Anthropic + OpenAI + Zhipu + MiniMax beats four models from one lab):
    60	
    61	```bash
    62	MODELS="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5,openai/gpt-5.1,z-ai/glm-5.2" jury.sh --commit HEAD
    63	```
    64	
    65	## Use it in Claude Code (skill or slash command)
    66	
    67	Make the jury part of your review workflow — Claude runs the panel and **triages** each finding
    68	(confirm or refute it against the actual code) instead of dumping raw model output. Two ways to
    69	install; pick one:
    70	
    71	**As a skill** (auto-discovered, model decides when to invoke it):
    72	```bash
    73	cp -r skills/ai-review-jury ~/.claude/skills/
    74	# then: set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your env, and edit the jury.sh path inside SKILL.md
    75	```
    76	
    77	**As a `/jury` slash command** (you invoke it explicitly):
    78	```bash
    79	mkdir -p ~/.claude/commands
    80	cp commands/jury.md ~/.claude/commands/jury.md
    81	# then: set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your env, and edit the jury.sh path inside it
    82	```
    83	
    84	Either way: in any repo, run it on your changes (`/jury`, `/jury --commit HEAD`, or
    85	`/jury focus on the auth changes`). A claim is a lead, not a verdict. Files:
    86	[`skills/ai-review-jury/SKILL.md`](skills/ai-review-jury/SKILL.md) ·
    87	[`commands/jury.md`](commands/jury.md).
    88	
    89	The non-code panel installs the same way: [`commands/panel.md`](commands/panel.md) →
    90	`~/.claude/commands/` for a `/panel` slash command, or
    91	[`skills/ai-review-panel/SKILL.md`](skills/ai-review-panel/SKILL.md) → `~/.claude/skills/`
    92	so the model reaches for it whenever an idea/plan/copy/spec critique fits.
    93	
    94	Confirm the install is wired, current, and live anytime (e.g. at session start):
    95	
    96	```bash
    97	bash /path/to/AI-Review-Jury/jury-check.sh
    98	# ✓ panel · ✓ key · ✓ /jury installed · ✓ repo live + in sync · ✓ freshness
    99	```
   100	
   101	## Beyond code: `panel.sh` — jury an idea, a plan, copy, or a UI spec
   102	
   103	The blind-spot thesis isn't code-specific. `panel.sh` runs the same diverse-lineage fan-out
   104	over **any text**, with a tuned critique prompt per preset and per-preset benchmarked seats
   105	read from `panels.conf`:
   106	
   107	```bash
   108	panel.sh --preset idea  pitch.md                 # unit economics, contradictions, regulatory, market math
   109	panel.sh --preset plan  rollout-plan.md "focus on rollback"   # ordering, races, missing rollback
   110	panel.sh --preset copy  landing-copy.md          # contradictory claims, legal risk, CTA mismatch
   111	panel.sh --preset design spec.md                 # a11y, overload, color-only state (TEXT specs, not screenshots)
   112	cat idea.md | panel.sh --preset idea -           # stdin
   113	```
   114	
   115	Seats are empirical here too — and they **don't transfer from the code benchmark**. In a
   116	48-planted-flaw benchmark across 10 models (fixtures with known arithmetic errors,
   117	contradictions, ordering bugs + clean controls to measure restraint): GLM-5.2 swept 48/48
   118	with zero false positives; the code panel's #2 (MiniMax) was mid-pack on prose; one large
   119	well-known model fabricated citations. Re-run it on your own fixtures: `panel-bench/collect.sh`
   120	→ judge with `panel-bench/judge-brief.md` → `panel-bench/aggregate.py` → edit `panels.conf`.
   121	Same contract as the jury: critics, never executors — findings are leads you triage.
   122	
   123	**`COUNCIL=1`** adds an anonymized cross-examination round (borrowed from Karpathy's
   124	[llm-council](https://github.com/karpathy/llm-council) Stage 2): each panelist must CONFIRM or
   125	REFUTE every finding the others made, with evidence, before your triage. Kills false positives
   126	early and makes panelists admit what they missed. Doubles the (tiny) cost.
   127	
   128	## Agentic mode: `agentic-juror.sh` — Codex-style review from a non-OpenAI lineage
   129	
   130	A diff-only jury can't read the caller in another file. `agentic-juror.sh` gives a foreign
   131	lineage the same repo-awareness OpenAI's Codex has, with zero extra accounts: it runs
   132	**headless Claude Code as the harness**, pointed at OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible
   133	endpoint (`/api/v1/messages` passes `tool_use` through), driving `z-ai/glm-5.2` read-only
   134	in your repo:
   135	
   136	```bash
   137	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... agentic-juror.sh <worktree-or-repo-path> <sha> /tmp/out
   138	# → /tmp/out.json (claude -p output) + /tmp/out.meta (cost, wall-clock, writes-check)
   139	```
   140	
   141	Measured on a 10-commit production bench (known ground truth): 10/10 loops completed,
   142	0 writes, ~150 well-formed tool calls, ~$0.46/review avg. It caught 3 real bugs the
   143	diff-only jury never produced (including one only found by tracing a *caller outside the
   144	diff*, and one by running the repo's own test suite) — and missed 2 the diff-only jury
   145	caught. **Same model, different mode = different blind spots: run it as a complement on
   146	high-stakes diffs, not a replacement.** Requires the `claude` CLI. Read-only is enforced
   147	via `--disallowedTools` deny rules; still verify the `writes_check` line in the meta output.
   148	
   149	## Benchmark: which models earn a seat?
   150	
   151	Don't take my table's word for it — your codebase is different. Run it on your own history:
   152	
   153	```bash
   154	cd /your/repo
   155	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... MODELS="z-ai/glm-5.2,minimax/minimax-m3,deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash" \
   156	  /path/to/AI-Review-Jury/bench/collect.sh 10          # 3 models × 10 recent commits
   157	```
   158	
   159	That writes one raw review per (commit, model) to `./ai-review-jury-bench/reviews/`. Now the part that makes it a *benchmark* and not a vibe: **triage every finding against the real code** and write one verdict JSON per commit (see [`bench/judge-brief.md`](bench/judge-brief.md) — you can do this by hand, or hand each commit to a strong judge model). Then:
   160	
   161	```bash
   162	python3 /path/to/AI-Review-Jury/bench/aggregate.py ./ai-review-jury-bench/verdicts
   163	```
   164	
   165	→ the precision/recall/unique-REAL scorecard above, for **your** code. Keep the models that pull their weight; drop the ones that just fill your inbox.
   166	
   167	## Self-updating (the panel tunes itself)
   168	
   169	A frozen panel rots — new models ship weekly. So after a week, `jury.sh` nudges you:
   170	
   171	```
   172	◆ ⚠ Panel is 8d old — new models may have shipped. Re-benchmark + self-update: run jury-tune (or /jury-tune)
   173	```
   174	
   175	Running **`jury-tune`** (or the `/jury-tune` skill in Claude Code) then does, automatically, what you'd do by hand:
   176	
   177	1. `tune-collect.sh` fetches the live OpenRouter model list, picks the current panel + the newest plausible-reviewer model **per lineage since your last tune**, and benchmarks them all over your recent diffs.
   178	2. The skill **verifies every finding against your actual code** (real vs false positive — establishing ground truth on the fly, since recent diffs aren't pre-labelled), scoring each candidate on **unique verified-real bugs** vs **false positives**.
   179	3. It rewrites `panel.conf` **only if a challenger genuinely earns a seat** — caught a real bug the incumbents missed, at no worse a false-positive rate. A model that fired confident false alarms, came back empty, or timed out is never seated, no matter its raw catch count. Then it stamps `.jury-last-tuned`.
   180	
   181	**"No change" is the common, correct outcome** — the bar to swap the models reviewing your code is deliberately high. `panel.conf` and `.jury-last-tuned` are per-user (gitignored); the shipped default (`glm-5.2 + minimax-m3`) is the fallback.
   182	
   183	## What this is not
   184	
   185	- **Not an auto-fixer.** It never touches your code. Findings are leads to verify.
   186	- **Not a replacement for your own review or CI.** It's a cheap extra set of differently-blind eyes on high-stakes diffs (money, auth, security, migrations).
   187	- **Not magic.** Models still miss bugs and still hallucinate them. The benchmark exists precisely so you can measure that instead of trusting a marketing table.
   188	
   189	## The bigger lever
   190	
   191	The highest-leverage upgrade isn't a fourth model — it's making every finding **prove itself**: require a claimed bug to ship a failing test/repro before you act on it. That converts an N-model vote into hard signal and kills the false-positive triage tax. `AI Review Jury` is the cheap first step (diverse eyes); execution-grounded verification is the next one.
   192	
   193	## License
   194	
   195	MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

     5	
     6	# AI Review Jury
     7	
     8	A panel of diverse-lineage AI models reviews the current diff; you then triage each finding
     9	against the real code. Different training lineages have different blind spots, so the panel
    10	catches bugs any single reviewer — including your own Claude session — misses. It never edits
    11	code: findings are leads, not verdicts.
    12	
    13	## Setup (once)
    14	- Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the environment (from https://openrouter.ai/keys) — one key covers
    15	  every model lineage (Claude, GPT, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek); no separate accounts.
    16	- Clone https://github.com/SignalEngine/AI-Review-Jury and note the path to `jury.sh` (or put it on PATH).
    17	
    18	## Run it
    19	From inside the repo you're reviewing (read-only):
    20	```bash

    22	bash /path/to/AI-Review-Jury/jury.sh --commit <sha>
    23	bash /path/to/AI-Review-Jury/jury.sh --uncommitted "focus on the auth + payment changes"
    24	```
    25	- Each model is a parallel OpenRouter request. A slow *reasoning* model in the panel can take a
    26	  few minutes — use a large Bash timeout (e.g. 360000ms) or run it in the background and read the
    27	  output when it lands.
    28	- Panel is `MODELS=`-overridable. **Running inside Claude?** Drop Claude from the panel — your
    29	  session already is a Claude reviewer — and spend those slots on non-Claude lineages for maximum
    30	  non-overlapping coverage. Which models earn a seat is empirical: benchmark them with `bench/`.
    31	
    32	## Triage — this is the skill, not the model output
    33	The models will AGREE and DISAGREE — that's the value. For every distinct finding:
    34	- Open the cited file/line and **confirm or refute it against the actual code**. A model lacks
    35	  your session's context; some findings are stale, out of scope, or wrong.
    36	- When two models disagree about the same code, look HARDER there — do not average them.
    37	- Label each **Confirmed** / **Refuted** (with the reason) / **Style**. Note which model(s)
    38	  caught each real bug.
    39	
    40	## Report
    41	State which diff was reviewed, then Confirmed issues first (most severe first, each with
    42	file:line evidence), then a short list of what you refuted and why. Don't auto-apply fixes
    43	unless asked. After fixing Confirmed P1s, re-run to confirm they're resolved.

+# 5. the private-file push guard is ACTIVE, not merely present in the tree.
+# Git never auto-runs hooks from a clone (deliberate, and no repo content can change

+Z0=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
+probe_blocks(){ ! _feed refs/heads/p 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 refs/heads/p 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222; }

+fi

index 0000000..50ebe20
--- /dev/null
+++ b/idea-panel.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# idea-panel.sh — the divergence-map front end for an idea/plan.
+#
+# Not "N models critique in parallel" (that's panel.sh). This surfaces WHERE
+# diverse perspectives DISAGREE — because disagreement is the signal worth
+# researching. Pipeline:
+#   0. LEDGER FIRST — brain-search the idea's terms; a prior verdict beats a
+#      fresh debate (the 2026-07-24 lesson: the vault already had the answer).
+#   1. Three ROLE-diverse, LINEAGE-diverse perspectives: advocate / skeptic /
+#      researcher (role framing changes output — proven in the bake-off).
+#   2. Synthesis into a DIVERGENCE MAP: consensus | disagreements+crux | unknowns.
+#   3. Append to the idea-ledger for later preference/reliability learning.
+#
+# Usage:  idea-panel.sh idea.md ["optional focus"]
+#         echo "my idea..." | idea-panel.sh -
+#
+# Env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (req). MODELS_ADVOCATE/SKEPTIC/RESEARCHER/SYNTH override roles.
+set -euo pipefail
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
+[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+SRC="${1:--}"; FOCUS="${2:-}"
+CONTENT="$([ "$SRC" = "-" ] && cat || cat "$SRC")"
+[ -n "$CONTENT" ] || { echo "✗ empty idea" >&2; exit 1; }
+MAX=${MAX_CHARS:-40000}; CONTENT="${CONTENT:0:$MAX}"
+
+# Role→model. Candidates (deepseek-v4-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite) sit in the
+# generative roles so each run measures their PLANNING signal; the proven
+# critic/synth models (minimax, glm) hold the judgement seats.
+M_ADV="${MODELS_ADVOCATE:-deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash}"
+M_SKEP="${MODELS_SKEPTIC:-minimax/minimax-m3}"
+M_RES="${MODELS_RESEARCHER:-google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite}"
+M_SYNTH="${MODELS_SYNTH:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
+
+call() { # model, prompt  ->  text
+  local model="$1" prompt="$2" req
+  req=$(python3 -c '
+import json,sys
+print(json.dumps({"model":sys.argv[3],"temperature":0,
+  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":sys.argv[1]+"\n\n--- IDEA ---\n"+sys.argv[2]}]}))' \
+    "$prompt" "$CONTENT" "$model")
+  curl -s -m "${PANEL_TIMEOUT:-240}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -H "X-Title: idea-panel" -d "$req" | python3 -c '
+import json,sys
+raw=sys.stdin.read()
+try: d=json.loads(raw)
+except Exception: print("(non-JSON response)"); sys.exit(1)
+if isinstance(d,dict) and d.get("error"): print("(model error:",d["error"],")"); sys.exit(1)
+try:
+  m=d["choices"][0]["message"]; body=m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning")
+  if not body: print("(empty response)"); sys.exit(1)
+  print(body)
+except Exception: print("(bad shape:",raw[:200],")"); sys.exit(1)'
+}
+
+FOCUS_LINE="${FOCUS:+ The user asks you to focus on: $FOCUS.}"
+P_ADV="You are an ADVOCATE. You believe this idea can work. Give the STRONGEST version: the core mechanism, why it succeeds, the best realistic path to make it real, and the one thing that most makes it worth doing. Be concrete, not cheerleading.$FOCUS_LINE"
+P_SKEP="You are a SKEPTIC. You think this idea is likely flawed. Find the CONCRETE reasons it fails: unit-economics that don't add up (do the math), internal contradictions, hidden costs, false assumptions, why it won't work as imagined, simpler things that already solve it. No vague doubts — specific failure modes only.$FOCUS_LINE"
+P_RES="You are a RESEARCHER. Do NOT judge good/bad. Identify what is UNKNOWN: the load-bearing ASSUMPTIONS that need checking, the QUESTIONS whose answers would flip the verdict, and for each, HOW to find the answer (what to test, measure, or look up). Rank by how much the answer would change the decision.$FOCUS_LINE"
+
+echo "◆ idea-panel: ledger → advocate($M_ADV) · skeptic($M_SKEP) · researcher($M_RES) → divergence map" >&2
+
+# ── 0. LEDGER FIRST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+echo "═══ 0 · PRIOR KNOWLEDGE (brain-search) ═══"
+TERMS=$(python3 -c '
+import re,sys,collections
+stop=set("this that with have from your will they them then than into over about which what when where would could should being your yours idea plan system user users".split())
+w=[x.lower() for x in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]{5,}", sys.stdin.read())]
+c=collections.Counter(x for x in w if x not in stop)
+print(" ".join(t for t,_ in c.most_common(4)))' <<<"$CONTENT")
+echo "  terms: $TERMS"
+python3 /root/.claude/scripts/brain-search.py -n 4 $TERMS 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /' || echo "  (no ledger hits)"
+
+# Prior DECISIONS (your logged picks + why) — the taste signal fed into synthesis.
+PRIOR_DECISIONS="$(grep -A2 '^### DECISION' "$HERE/idea-ledger.md" 2>/dev/null | tail -40 || true)"
+[ -n "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" ] && { echo; echo "  prior decisions on record (feeding synthesis):"; echo "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" | sed 's/^/    /'; }
+
+# ── 1. THREE ROLE-DIVERSE PERSPECTIVES (parallel) ────────────────────────────
+TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+( call "$M_ADV"  "$P_ADV"  > "$TMP/adv"  2>&1 || touch "$TMP/adv.fail"  ) &
+( call "$M_SKEP" "$P_SKEP" > "$TMP/skep" 2>&1 || touch "$TMP/skep.fail" ) &
+( call "$M_RES"  "$P_RES"  > "$TMP/res"  2>&1 || touch "$TMP/res.fail"  ) &
+wait
+echo; echo "═══ 1 · PERSPECTIVES ═══"
+for r in "ADVOCATE:$M_ADV:adv" "SKEPTIC:$M_SKEP:skep" "RESEARCHER:$M_RES:res"; do
+  IFS=: read -r label model file <<<"$r"
+  echo; echo "── $label ($model) ──"; cat "$TMP/$file"
+done
+
+# A map synthesized from error strings is indistinguishable from a real one once
+# it is in the ledger. If any perspective failed, stop here (review-gate P2, 07-27).
+if compgen -G "$TMP/*.fail" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo >&2; echo "✗ perspective(s) FAILED above — refusing to synthesize a divergence map" >&2
+  echo "  from error text, and NOT appending to the ledger." >&2; exit 1
+fi
+
+# ── 2. DIVERGENCE MAP ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# %s not %b: model output is untrusted and %b would interpret its backslash
+# escapes — a returned "\\c" truncates the bundle silently. (review-gate P2, 07-27)
+BUNDLE="$(printf 'ADVOCATE said:\n%s\n\nSKEPTIC said:\n%s\n\nRESEARCHER said:\n%s\n' \
+  "$(cat "$TMP/adv")" "$(cat "$TMP/skep")" "$(cat "$TMP/res")")"
+P_SYNTH="Below are three perspectives (advocate/skeptic/researcher) on the same idea. Produce a DIVERGENCE MAP, nothing else:
+1. CONSENSUS — points all three implicitly agree on (the safe ground).
+2. DISAGREEMENTS — where they genuinely conflict. For EACH, state the CRUX: the single question whose answer decides who is right.
+3. TOP UNKNOWNS TO RESEARCH — ranked by how much resolving them would change the decision; name the concrete check for each.
+Be terse and concrete. Do not re-argue the idea; map the structure of the disagreement.${PRIOR_DECISIONS:+
+
+The user has made these PRIOR DECISIONS on related ideas (their taste signal) — weight the map toward what they have valued, and FLAG if this idea repeats or contradicts a past decision:
+$PRIOR_DECISIONS}"
+echo; echo "═══ 2 · DIVERGENCE MAP ($M_SYNTH) ═══"
+MAP=$(call "$M_SYNTH" "$BUNDLE
+
+$P_SYNTH") || {
+  echo "✗ synthesis failed — NOT appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "$MAP"
+
+# ── 3. LEDGER APPEND (capture for later learning) ────────────────────────────
+LEDGER="$HERE/idea-ledger.md"
+{ echo; echo "## $(head -1 <<<"$CONTENT" | sed 's/^#* *//' | cut -c1-80) — logged"
+  echo "_models: adv=$M_ADV skep=$M_SKEP res=$M_RES synth=${M_SYNTH}_"
+  echo "$MAP"; echo "---"; } >> "$LEDGER" || { echo "✗ ledger append FAILED — not reporting success" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo; echo "◆ appended to $LEDGER (add your pick + why later → feeds preference learning)" >&2

index 0000000..38ed0c8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/idea-options.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# idea-options.sh — the GENERATE stage the planning pipeline was missing.
+#
+# idea-panel.sh answers "is this idea any good?" — its three roles (advocate,
+# skeptic, researcher) all REACT to the solution you hand them, so by
+# construction it can never tell you there is a better idea. That gap was found
+# on 2026-07-25: asked for an alternative to a proposed mobile UI, the pipeline
+# had no seat for one and produced only a critique of the original.
+#
+# This script takes the PROBLEM and produces DIVERGENT APPROACHES to it:
+#   0. brain-search prior knowledge + read the decision ledger (your taste)
+#   1. N proposers, different lineages, IN PARALLEL and blind to each other —
+#      each must propose ONE approach in a fixed shape. If the problem statement
+#      names a solution already, they are required to propose a DIFFERENT one.
+#   2. one judge scores every option on the same rubric and ranks them
+#   3. synthesis: a recommendation, what to graft from the runners-up, and the
+#      checks to run before committing
+#   4. append to the shared idea-ledger
+#
+# Usage:  idea-options.sh problem.md ["optional focus"]
+#         echo "the problem..." | idea-options.sh -
+#
+# Then log your pick:  idea-decide "<ref>" "<what you chose and why>"
+#
+# Env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY (req). MODELS_PROPOSERS (comma-sep) / MODELS_JUDGE /
+#      MODELS_SYNTH override the defaults. PANEL_TIMEOUT (default 240s).
+set -uo pipefail
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
+[ -n "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+SRC="${1:--}"; FOCUS="${2:-}"
+CONTENT="$([ "$SRC" = "-" ] && cat || cat "$SRC")"
+[ -n "$CONTENT" ] || { echo "✗ empty problem statement" >&2; exit 1; }
+MAX=${MAX_CHARS:-40000}; CONTENT="${CONTENT:0:$MAX}"
+
+# Proposers sit in cheap/diverse seats (their job is RANGE, not judgement);
+# the proven judge model holds the scoring seat, same split as idea-panel.
+IFS=, read -r -a PROPOSERS <<< "${MODELS_PROPOSERS:-deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash,google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite,minimax/minimax-m3}"
+M_JUDGE="${MODELS_JUDGE:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
+M_SYNTH="${MODELS_SYNTH:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
+
+call() { # model, prompt  ->  text   (verbatim from idea-panel.sh — same wire shape)
+  local model="$1" prompt="$2" req
+  req=$(python3 -c '
+import json,sys
+print(json.dumps({"model":sys.argv[3],"temperature":0,
+  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":sys.argv[1]+"\n\n--- PROBLEM ---\n"+sys.argv[2]}]}))' \
+    "$prompt" "$CONTENT" "$model")
+  curl -s -m "${PANEL_TIMEOUT:-240}" https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -H "X-Title: idea-options" -d "$req" | python3 -c '
+import json,sys
+raw=sys.stdin.read()
+try: d=json.loads(raw)
+except Exception: print("(non-JSON response)"); sys.exit(1)
+if isinstance(d,dict) and d.get("error"): print("(model error:",d["error"],")"); sys.exit(1)
+try:
+  m=d["choices"][0]["message"]; body=m.get("content") or m.get("reasoning")
+  if not body: print("(empty response)"); sys.exit(1)
+  print(body)
+except Exception: print("(bad shape:",raw[:200],")"); sys.exit(1)'
+}
+
+FOCUS_LINE="${FOCUS:+ Focus on: $FOCUS.}"
+
+# The fixed output shape is what makes options comparable — a judge cannot rank
+# free-form prose on the same axes.
+SHAPE='Answer in EXACTLY this shape, once:
+
+### OPTION: <short distinctive name>
+MECHANISM: <how it actually works, concretely — name the moving parts>
+WHY IT FITS: <why this solves the stated problem, not a nearby one>
+COST: <build effort + ongoing cost; be honest about the expensive part>
+BREAKS/RISKS: <what this makes worse, who it hurts, what could regress>
+REVERSIBILITY: <how hard to undo once shipped>
+EVIDENCE NEEDED: <the check that would confirm this is the right call>'
+
+P_PROPOSE="You are a solution ARCHITECT. Propose ONE approach that solves the PROBLEM below.
+
+HARD RULES:
+- Solve the PROBLEM, not a nearby or easier one.
+- If the problem statement mentions a solution someone already proposed, you MUST propose a DIFFERENT approach. Do not endorse, restate, or merely refine theirs.
+- Do NOT critique other approaches. Do NOT hedge with several options. ONE approach, committed to.
+- Prefer approaches that a small team can ship. Name the cheapest version that still solves it.
+- No filler. If a section is genuinely 'none', say none.${FOCUS_LINE}
+
+$SHAPE"
+
+echo "◆ idea-options: ledger → ${#PROPOSERS[@]} blind proposers → judge($M_JUDGE) → synthesis" >&2
+
+# ── 0. PRIOR KNOWLEDGE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+echo "═══ 0 · PRIOR KNOWLEDGE (brain-search) ═══"
+TERMS=$(python3 -c '
+import re,sys,collections
+stop=set("this that with have from your will they them then than into over about which what when where would could should being your yours idea plan system user users problem".split())
+w=[x.lower() for x in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]{5,}", sys.stdin.read())]
+c=collections.Counter(x for x in w if x not in stop)
+print(" ".join(t for t,_ in c.most_common(4)))' <<<"$CONTENT")
+echo "  terms: $TERMS"
+python3 /root/.claude/scripts/brain-search.py -n 4 $TERMS 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /' || echo "  (no ledger hits)"
+
+PRIOR_DECISIONS="$(grep -A2 '^### DECISION' "$HERE/idea-ledger.md" 2>/dev/null | tail -40 || true)"
+[ -n "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" ] && { echo; echo "  prior decisions on record (feeding synthesis):"; echo "$PRIOR_DECISIONS" | sed 's/^/    /'; }
+
+# ── 1. BLIND PROPOSERS (parallel) ────────────────────────────────────────────
+TMP=$(mktemp -d) || TMP=""
+{ [ -n "$TMP" ] && [ -d "$TMP" ]; } || { echo "✗ mktemp -d failed — refusing to run" >&2; exit 2; }; trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+i=0
+for m in "${PROPOSERS[@]}"; do
+  i=$((i+1))
+  ( call "$m" "$P_PROPOSE" > "$TMP/opt$i" 2>&1 || touch "$TMP/opt$i.fail" ) &
+done
+wait
+
+echo; echo "═══ 1 · OPTIONS (each proposed blind) ═══"
+i=0; BUNDLE=""
+for m in "${PROPOSERS[@]}"; do
+  i=$((i+1))
+  echo; echo "── proposer $i ($m) ──"; cat "$TMP/opt$i"
+  BUNDLE="$BUNDLE
+
+=== FROM PROPOSER $i ($m) ===
+$(cat "$TMP/opt$i")"
+done
+
+# ── 2. JUDGE — same rubric applied to every option ───────────────────────────
+P_JUDGE="Below are independently-proposed approaches to the same problem.
+
+First, MERGE duplicates: if two proposers describe the same approach, treat them as one option and say so. Genuinely distinct approaches stay separate.
+
+Then score EVERY surviving option 1-5 on each axis, with a one-line reason per score:
+- FIT — does it solve the stated problem, or a nearby easier one?
+- COST — build + ongoing (5 = cheap)
+- REVERSIBILITY — how easily undone (5 = trivial to undo)
+- CONFIDENCE — how much do we already know this works, vs needing evidence?
+
+Then rank them by total, and state in one line WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE for the bottom-ranked option to beat the top one. Be terse. Do not invent new options."
+
+echo; echo "═══ 2 · SCORED ($M_JUDGE) ═══"
+if compgen -G "$TMP/*.fail" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo >&2; echo "✗ proposer(s) FAILED above — refusing to judge/rank error text," >&2
+  echo "  and NOT appending to the ledger." >&2; exit 1
+fi
+SCORES=$(call "$M_JUDGE" "$(printf '%s' "$BUNDLE")
+
+$P_JUDGE") || { echo "✗ judge failed — NOT ranking or appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "$SCORES"
+
+# ── 3. SYNTHESIS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+P_SYNTH="You have independently-proposed options and a judge's scoring of them.
+
+Produce, terse:
+1. RECOMMENDATION — one option, and the single strongest reason it wins.
+2. GRAFT — the best specific idea from a NON-winning option that should be folded into the winner.
+3. DO NOT BUILD — any option that looks attractive but should be rejected, and why in one line.
+4. BEFORE COMMITTING — the concrete checks to run first (each must be mechanically checkable).
+Do not restate the options. Decide.${PRIOR_DECISIONS:+
+
+The user has made these PRIOR DECISIONS (their taste signal) — weight toward what they have valued, and FLAG if a recommendation contradicts one:
+$PRIOR_DECISIONS}"
+
+echo; echo "═══ 3 · SYNTHESIS ($M_SYNTH) ═══"
+OUT=$(call "$M_SYNTH" "$(printf '%s' "$BUNDLE")
+
+JUDGE SAID:
+$SCORES
+
+$P_SYNTH") || { echo "✗ synthesis failed — NOT appending to the ledger" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "$OUT"
+
+# ── 4. LEDGER ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+LEDGER="$HERE/idea-ledger.md"
+{ echo; echo "## OPTIONS — $(head -1 <<<"$CONTENT" | sed 's/^#* *//' | cut -c1-80)"
+  echo "_proposers: ${PROPOSERS[*]} · judge=$M_JUDGE · synth=${M_SYNTH}_"
+  echo "$SCORES"; echo; echo "$OUT"; echo "---"; } >> "$LEDGER" || { echo "✗ ledger append FAILED — not reporting success" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo; echo "◆ appended to $LEDGER — log your pick with: idea-decide \"<ref>\" \"<choice + why>\"" >&2

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# pre-push — refuse to publish per-user private notes to a PUBLIC remote.
+#
+# Why a hook and not just .gitignore: untracking a file at HEAD does NOT remove it
+# from older commits. idea-ledger.md was untracked at the tip on 2026-07-27 while two
+# unpushed commits still carried the blob — one `git push` would have published it.
+# So this checks every commit in the push RANGE, not just the tip.
+#
+# INSTALL (git never auto-runs hooks from a clone — this is a git security property,
+# not an oversight here):  git config core.hooksPath hooks
+# jury-check.sh reports every session whether this guard is actually active.
+#
+# ponytail: one explicit list, no config file. Add names to PRIVATE as they appear.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+# git passes <remote-name> <remote-url>. Excluding commits present on a hardcoded
+# "origin" is wrong when pushing to a DIFFERENT remote: with an internal origin and
+# a public remote, everything already on origin was skipped and the private file
+# published (review-gate P1, 07-27). An unknown/URL remote matches no refs, so the
+# scan widens rather than narrows — the safe direction.
+REMOTE="${1:-origin}"
+
+# Match the BASENAME at ANY depth, because .gitignore does: a bare pattern with no
+# slash is ignored at every level, so notes/idea-ledger.md is private to git but was
+# publishable by this guard — the exact inverse of the round-1 claim I refuted.
+PRIVATE='(^|/)(idea-ledger\.md|[^/]*\.private\.md)$'
+Z=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
+bad=0
+
+while read -r _lref lsha _rref rsha; do
+  [ "$lsha" = "$Z" ] && continue                      # branch deletion — nothing to inspect
+  # FAIL CLOSED. Discarding rev-list's exit status made this guard fail OPEN: an
+  # advertised remote SHA that is not present locally (shallow / partial fetch)
+  # makes rev-list exit 128, the commit list comes back empty, the loop never
+  # runs, and a push carrying private notes is ALLOWED. Caught by review-gate
+  # 2026-07-27 by executing it, not by reading it. An unknown range is not an
+  # empty range — if we cannot enumerate what is being pushed, we refuse.
+  if [ "$rsha" = "$Z" ]; then
+    # Scan EVERYTHING reachable. Excluding commits that local remote-tracking refs
+    # claim are already published is unsound: those refs go stale, and survive the
+    # remote being repointed at a different URL — so a commit "already on origin"
+    # may never have been on THIS remote. Reproduced by review-gate, 07-27.
+    # ponytail: O(history) per new-branch push; fine at this repo's size. If it ever
+    # matters, ask the remote itself with ls-remote rather than trusting local refs.
+    raw="$(git rev-list "$lsha" 2>&1)" || raw="!"
+  else
+    raw="$(git rev-list "$rsha..$lsha" 2>&1)" || raw="!"
+  fi
+  if [ "$raw" = "!" ]; then
+    printf '✗ pre-push BLOCKED — cannot enumerate the push range (%s..%s).\n' "${rsha:0:7}" "${lsha:0:7}" >&2
+    printf '      Refusing rather than assuming it is empty. Try: git fetch origin\n' >&2
+    bad=1; continue
+  fi
+  mapfile -t commits <<< "$raw"
+  for c in "${commits[@]}"; do
+    [ -n "$c" ] || continue
+    # -z: git C-QUOTES non-ASCII/special names by default ("\345\256\242...\.md"),
+    # which the regex misses — a real leak path for e.g. 客户.private.md.
+    # NUL-delimited output is raw. (review-gate P1, 07-27)
+    # tr INSIDE the pipeline: bash command substitution silently strips NUL bytes,
+    # so capturing -z output directly concatenates every path into one line and the
+    # anchored regex stops matching. pipefail carries an ls-tree failure out.
+    if ! tree="$(git ls-tree -r -z --name-only "$c" 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n')"; then
+      printf '✗ pre-push BLOCKED — cannot read the tree of %s; refusing to assume it is clean\n' "${c:0:7}" >&2
+      bad=1; continue
+    fi
+    hits="$(printf '%s\n' "$tree" | grep -E "$PRIVATE" || true)"
+    if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
+      printf '✗ pre-push BLOCKED — %s carries private file(s):\n' "${c:0:7}" >&2
+      printf '%s\n' "$hits" | sed 's/^/      /' >&2
+      bad=1
+    fi
+  done
+done
+
+if [ "$bad" != 0 ]; then
+  cat >&2 <<'MSG'
+
+  This remote is PUBLIC. Untracking the file at HEAD is not enough — the blob is
+  still in the commits being pushed. Drop it from the range first, e.g.:
+
+    git filter-branch --index-filter 'git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch <file>' <upstream>..HEAD
+
+  where <upstream> is what you are pushing against (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u}).
+
+  Then push again. To bypass deliberately: git push --no-verify (think first).
+MSG
+  exit 1
+fi
+exit 0

 MODEL="${MODEL:-z-ai/glm-5.2}"
+export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-$(/root/.local/bin/ork 2>/dev/null)}"
 KEY="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}"
 MAX="${MAX_DIFF_CHARS:-120000}"
 [ -n "$KEY" ] || { echo "✗ OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set" >&2; exit 1; }

 OUT="${OUT:-./jury-tune-run}"

superpowers:using-superpowers\n- superpowers:verification-before-completion\n- superpowers:writing-plans\n- superpowers:writing-skills\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- init\n- superpowers:using-superpowers\n- superpowers:verification-before-completion\n- superpowers:writing-plans\n- superpowers:writing-skills\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- init\n- /root/.claude/projects/-root-wt-calcom/5159ba62-2c19-4802-bcdc-01aae99f6815.jsonl:10:{"parentUuid":"a12cf8c9-db0f-43c2-907f-b818f9a6cae9","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- ab-test-setup\n- analytics-tracking\n- brain: Use when recalling project knowledge — \"did we hit this before\", \"where is X documented\", \"how did we fix/decide Y\", looking for a past root cause, checking vault docs before asking James for context, or when about to grep/read many vault or memory files to find one fact.\n- competitor-alternatives\n- content-strategy\n- copy-editing\n- copywriting\n- design-verify: Use after building or changing ANY UI (lander, dashboard, component, value page) before claiming it's done — or when asked to review/verify a design, check a page visually, or confirm animations work. Replaces \"Read the PNG and judge\" with deterministic checks + a fresh-context rubric verdict.\n- email-sequence\n- engine-doctor: Use for an engine health pass — \"run the doctor\", periodic checkups, after remediations, or when something feels off fleet-wide. Covers vitals, pipeline economics, sending capacity, campaign state, AND Hive QA (audit + probe). Complements /engine-lore (debugging lore for a specific fault).\n- engine-lore: Use when working on SignalEngine containers, deploys, or diagnostics — engine health/watchdog reports, reprovisioning, phase gating/calendar issues, prospect queues stalling, contact verification/bounces, \"why isn't phase X running\", subagent hallucinations about missing tools, authed /my-engine headless snapshots, or reading errors24h/errors30m counts. Holds the hard-won operational lore migrated from CLAUDE.md (2026-07-03 diet).\n- fable-mode: Use when the user says \"fable mode\", \"fable\", \"think like fable\", \"operate like fable\", or asks for higher-rigor judgement, planning, verification, or reasoning discipline on any task. Also use at the start of complex, ambiguous, or multi-step work where sloppy verification or premature conclusions would be costly.\n- form-cro\n- free-tool-strategy\n- gate: Use BEFORE building a feature when the definition of done can be checked mechanically — designs an executable acceptance gate FIRST (baseline must fail RED), then the build loops until the gate passes. Trigger on \"/gate\", \"gate this\", \"acceptance gate\", or when starting feature work where \"done\" keeps slipping. Adapted from fusion-harness's auto-validate loop.\n- herdr: Control Herdr, a terminal multiplexer for coding agents. Use only when the user explicitly mentions Herdr or asks to use Herdr to inspect or control panes, tabs, workspaces, commands, or another agent. Do not use merely because a task could benefit from a background terminal, delegation, or parallel work. Requires HERDR_ENV=1.\n- hive-audit: Use when James asks to check Hive conversations for problems (\"run the hive audit\", \"any issues in hive?\", \"check what users are hitting in the hive\"), after shipping Hive/chat-tool changes to see real-world effect, or on a periodic health pass. Pulls recent Hive conversations from ALL prod tenants (IMT, SignalEngine, LaunchEngine users, etc.), builds a flagged digest, and drives a triage.\n- hive-probe: Use to ACTIVELY test the Hive — inject a battery of read-only prompts as real chat turns and grade the replies against ground truth. Run after any Hive-touching deploy (tools, prompts, engineChat), when James asks \"test the hive\", or paired with /hive-audit (passive) for a full check. Injection primitive also usable ad-hoc to ask Hive one-off questions programmatically.\n- impeccable: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary.
